items.sum: Report and result of the R.W.A. 20 miles walk at Chiswick, where Belgrave lost the team title to Sheffield by one point but won the Nijmegen shield for the seventh year, with Ray Middleton third.
items.s: THE R.W.A. 20 MILES: Team Race decided in final few yards. Report and result of the R.W.A. 20 miles walk at Chiswick, where Belgrave lost the team title to Sheffield by one point but won the Nijmegen shield for the seventh year, with Ray Middleton third. In yet another very close team contest Belgrave had to relinquish their hold on a second "National" trophy by the narrow margin of 1 point. Held in very warm weather over a fast course at Chiswick, this year's entries included Olympic Gold Medallist Don Thompson and a strong East-German contingent. Thompson and Koch fought a bitter battle for 15 miles, before the German was ruled out when 50 yards in arrears. Ray Middleton and Eric Hall were once more spearheading the Belgrave team effort, being well up amongst the first six. Ken Bailey and George Beecham were also showing good form in the twenties. For a large part of the race Leicester were leading in the team placings from ourselves and Sheffield, but they gradually lost their grip and it looked very much as though we would scape home, but a gradual improvement over the last few miles by Sheffield and the weakening of a very gallant George Beecham (passed in the last 250 yards) combined to give Sheffield a single point advantage. Yet again we must report that Ray Middleton produced his best ever performance. This was his first "place" in a National event and it should not be long before his first win is recorded. Eric Hall just can't be kept away from the leading positions and, in the circumstances, his 6th position was an admirable effort. Belgrave's depth is illustrated once more by our winning of the Nijmegen shield for seventh consecutive year. Awarded to the Club with their eight men home first, it was indeed gladdening to see us finish ten men before our nearest rivals could find the required eight. Pos Name (Club) Time 1. D. items.s: BELS. RETAIN R.W.A. 50 KILOS Report and result of the R.W.A. 50 km walk, in which Belgrave retained the team title and Ray Middleton finished second to Don Thompson in a club record. Having narrowly lost two of their three National titles our boys were determined to hold on to this, the last. And hold it they did. For although they were without Bailey, McGreechan and Yescombe they had three men home before any club could finish two. There was no doubt about this team result! Once more honours go to Ray Middleton who moved up yet again in his National placings, finishing second to Olympic Gold Medallist Don Thompson, and setting a new Club record in his first 50 kilos! Ray was the only walker to make Thompson look beatable, and now has placings of 5th, 3rd and 2nd in the year's three premier events. He is surely on the threshold of achieving high honours. Ray Hall and George Beecham were always well placed and provided the backing for team honours. John Keown walked well to complete our scoring four and was closely followed by D. Bartliff and J. Morris. These three had had a race battle for 4th place and it was only in the last mile that John asserted his position. Special thanks are due to Mavis and Eric Hall for the assistance they provided with a car during the race. Jack Goswell says he would never have been able to give the necessary attentions to our team without their help. Pos Name (Club) Time 1. D. Thompson (Met. W.C.) 4:22:51 2. R. items.s: THE INTER-CLUB WALKS Report and results of the Inter-Club Walks at Battersea Park track on 5 July 1961, where Belgrave finished second of twelve clubs to Metropolitan W.C. Eighty-seven competitors took part in this year's contest, held at Battersea Park track on Wednesday July 5th. This was the largest number since the meeting's inauguration in 1953. Met. items.label: July 1961
items.sum: M.E.R.'s review of the 1961 track season so far: the Eldridge-Morris quarter-mile rivalry, new club records by Bob Norton (880) and Bill Kerr (2 miles), the weak sprint and field events sections, and results of six inter-club matches (continued on page 21).
items.s: TRACK ROUND-UP M.E.R.'s review of the 1961 track season so far: the Eldridge-Morris quarter-mile rivalry, new club records by Bob Norton (880) and Bill Kerr (2 miles), the weak sprint and field events sections, and results of six inter-club matches (continued on page 21). The highlight of this season, so far, is undoubtedly the struggle for supremacy between Peter Eldridge and Brian Morris, in the quarter-mile. After Peter's excellent start when taking third place in the Inter-counties, he looked to appear on top. But Brian, notorious for his slow first 220, relying on a fast last burst, ensured victory for Belgrave in the Continental Relay at the London Clubs' meeting at the White City. His 440 yards was clocked unofficially at 47.3 (!) and was followed a week later at Southampton when in the colours of Metropolitan Police he raced through the quarter again, in a Continental Relay, in 47.8. To crown it all he took fourth place in the A.A.A.'s final with 48.5 - after equalling the club record of 48.2 in his heat. Peter was pushed out in the semi-final with 49.0. Brian, Peter and Alan Secton now share this record; although Gerry Leroy's 47.7 400 metres must not be forgotten! South African Bob Norton is yet another member of the club to have run in the Inter-Versity match. Last year it was Rangit Bhatia in the mile; the year previous Clive Ryan in the 440. This year Bob ran in the event sandwiched by these two - the 880 yards. His 1:52.4, to win the Oxford University title, was a new Club Record. This time is exactly 3 seconds faster than our next fastest man this season, John Thresher, who ran 1:55.4 in the Ryder Trophy at Southampton. Another to establish a personal best at this event is Dave Mitchell. His 1:55.7 was accomplished with virtually no training - he has just graduated from College. A new face which has been of great help to us this season is that of Scotland's Bill Kerr. An athlete who suffers so little from nerves that either before or after a hard race he can still keep wisecracking, Bill came to us from Victoria Park four months ago, and has already set us a new Club Record in the 2 miles. His 8.55 when placed third in the London Club's 2 mile race at the White City erased Jack Brown's mark of 8.59 from the record book. Others to set up personal bests in this event are Malcolm Robinson with 9:08.2, Pat Newell 9:09, Dan Maclean 9:11.6 and John Davies 9:15. Malcolm, who lost his club mile title to John, is the fastest miler so far this season with 4:12.2, set in the Southern Championships, Bill Kerr is second with 4:16.0. Pat leads the list in the three mile with 14:00. This time was accomplished in the Middlesex Championships where he was placed 3rd - and was on a racing watch! Other more reliable watches had him inside the magical "14:00". In the six miles it is Malcolm again who leads, with 29:47.6. These five runners could well produce yet another record in the Club '3'. By the time this magazine has been distributed the result will be known - no prognostications from this writer! It is in the sprints that we are particularly weak. Apart from our quarter-miles we have none in action - save Graham Worrell, who defeated last year's Junion Champion John Strachan in the quarter-mile against Old Rutlishians. But then Graham is really a quarter-miler. He, together with Peter Eldridge, Brian Morris and Gerry Leroy (who clocked 48.9 when winning the Ryder Trophy event) could pull off the 4 x 440 A.A.A.'s title. However, the way seems very clear for almost any sprinter to assure the mantle of leading-sprinter. Not so many years ago we won the Sward Trophy for field events - in 1956, but now we are so lamentably poor in this section that we can't even field a team. Bill Couzens, now entering the marriage stakes, seemed at the beginning of the season to be in for a battle with George Edwards in the Javelin. This has not materialised, however, and despite his 167'0½" in the Kinnaird Bill has improved no further, mainly due to training difficulties, whilst George does not appear to be around much these days. There is an almost complete absence of men in the discus and shot. Roy Hollingsworth is only second claim for the discus and R. Shuter has no one to extend him in the shot. Of the remaining field events the long jump has the wealthiest look. Mick Smithers, in his first year as a Senior, has jumped 20'11" - with several over 21'0" disallowed, and Derek Wade (still a Junior) has leapt 20'8" - yet he has set his sights on breaking 2 minutes for the 'half'! Not so far behind is Heinz Leyer, who came to us at the beginning of the season from Germany - he has leapt 19'6" so far, but with the right encouragement this likeable and enthusiastic all-rounder could go much further. The season opened with a match against Ealing and Oxford City on April 4th, which we won. Our results were:- On 17th May Wimbledon, poor neighbours of Surrey (!) beat us 58 - 48:- Junior, Derek Wade, won the Long Jump 20'8". There were very few of our athletes at the match v Surrey, S.L.H., Wimbledon and Hercules at Norbiton on 6th June. John Thresher and Don Maclean continued their winning way. At Wimbledon Park on June 14th, Belgrave (67 points) were beaten in the senior match by Surrey A.C. (140), S.L.H. (122), and Wimbledon (105). It was on this evening that our Continental relay and 2 miles teams were running at Chiswick to qualify for the finals in the London Clubs White City Meeting. At Tooting Bec. on 19th June we had a match v St. Mary's College (60, S.L.H. (53), Old Rutlishians (30) - Belgrave scored 45 points. After toying with the field for two laps, Bill Kerr strode away for an easy victory in the 1 mile. Don Maclean was another to show a clean pair of heels to his opponents in the 2 miles. Third in this race was Ron Linstead, running for Old Rutlishians. Our persistent and enthusiastic Heinz Leyer at last won his first event - the high jump. In the Ryder Trophy held at Southampton, Gerry Leroy, was first in the 440 yards in 48.9 and John Thresher ran his personal best 880 in 1:55.4. On June 12th the match v Q.P.H. v St. Mary's College v Polytechnic was washed out. However, to placate the number who had turned out an "all-in" 880 was put on. This was won, from a field of 20 or so, by Youth David Cocks in 1:59.0!!! Our winning 4 x 110 yards relay team was the shock of the match against Woodford Green and the Army at Woodford on July 8th. The team comprised George Piddington, Don Newell, Cyril Forey & Ron Langheim. The Army, who were past the post first, were disqualified, and Woodford failed to finish. Earlier, Peter Pepe was narrowly defeated by the A.A.A.'s deathlaw Champion, Colin Andrews, in the quarter hurdles. The Army man clocked 57.3 to Peter's 57.4. In the 2 miles we were treated to the rare sight of John Davies setting the pace in a middle-distance race. And it payed off handsomely. He won in 9.15 - a time which is his best yet; better, indeed, than when 4.11 and 1.53 were common-place times to him! M.E.R. Event Pos Name Performance 100 yards 1. G. Leroy 10.5 220 yards 1. G. items.sum: Report of the 1961 Sward Trophy field events contest, where Belgrave came last of ten clubs, though Trevor Tolson and Peter Pepe did well in the hurdles and the relay team was second.
items.s: Sward trophy : Report of the 1961 Sward Trophy field events contest, where Belgrave came last of ten clubs, though Trevor Tolson and Peter Pepe did well in the hurdles and the relay team was second. Sponsored by Polytechnic Harriers, this meeting is the country's premier inter-club contest for field events. In 1956 we won the trophy, but in 1961 - only 5 years later - we were last of the ten competing clubs. However, our hurdlers did well. Trevor Tolson, after travelling all the way from Hull, took 4th place in the final of the 120 yards hurdles recording 16.0 seconds. Peter Pepe went one better in the final of the 440 yards hurdles, and but for "fluffing" the last hurdle would have been second; despite this he still recorded 59.2 seconds. Bill Couzens reached the final six in the javelin to qualify for another three throws, yet was not aware of this until too late! However, his 167'0½" in sixth place was a personal best. Mike Smithers, in the long jump, was also unfortunate. His 20'11½" failed to put him in the last six by just 1", and to think he had a jump of well over 21'0" disallowed - oh, well! In an Invitation Continental Relay we finished second to Polytechnic; our team of Leroy, Eldridge, Newell T., and Tolson recording 1:58.2 to Poly.'s 1:57.9. Pat Newell was our only man to show form in the Invitation 2 miles team race. He finished 7th in 9:09.0, but Bill Kerr had to retire after 5 laps with a troublesome injury and Robinson and Walker were nowhere near their best. We finished sixth of the eight teams. items.sum: Report of the Brockman Trophy at Croydon on 17 June 1961, a Herne Hill Harriers promotion, where Belgrave were the strongest track team but finished fifth through lack of field event points.
items.s: THE BROCKMAN TROPHY Report of the Brockman Trophy at Croydon on 17 June 1961, a Herne Hill Harriers promotion, where Belgrave were the strongest track team but finished fifth through lack of field event points. CROYDON, JUNE 17TH. Even though eleven clubs were competing in this Herne Hill Harriers promotion, Belgrave proved themselves to have the day's most powerful track team - yet they could only finish 5th in the final result! Why ? Well the composition of our score was as follows:- from 10 track events, 41 points; from 8 field events, 1 point. As we finished only 9 points behind the winners (T.V.H.) and 3 points behind the runners-up (Blackheath) we needed but a very modest score from the field to secure this important trophy. Needless to say, the team were very disappointed. We had two winners. Both were equally convincing. Peter Eldridge, running in the inside lane, had removed his stagger handicap before the runners had entered the third bend! He won by a good 15 yards in 49.0 seconds. Trevor Tolson was a clear winner in the high hurdles, recording 16.0 seconds against the wind. We had three runners-up. Most impressive of these was Bill Kerr, whose effort in the 3 miles showed what great potential he possesses. After nearly 2 miles of pace-setting by Stacey (T.V.H.), Bill with Longridge (S.L.H.) broke clear. With 660 yards to go our runner made his effort and managed to hold off his opponent's noted finish until the last 50 yards. Bill, by no means distressed, recorded a noteworthy 14:04.2, only 0.8 of a second down. Pat Newell's second place was gained in the six miles event. Card (T.V.H.) was a clear leader for 4 miles but faded badly enabling Pat, who had run a steady race, to gain just one more place and finish second in 30:10.2 - 18.6 seconds behind Major of Woodford. It was in the 3,000 metres Steeplechase that our third set of 5 points was gained. Clive Shippen set the pace from the start and by 2 laps had shaken off the last of the opposition. With 3 laps to go and a lead of 50 yards he seemed assured of 6 points, but Clive could not maintain the pace and, showing little fight, reliquished his lead at the bell to finish a thankful second with 9:49.0. We secured two third places. Gerry Leroy, still not entirely free of injury, managed to win his heat of the 100 yards; following this up with a fine 3rd place in the final, recording 10.4. And, in the final event of the day, our 4 x 440 yards relay team were just pushed out of second place by T.V.H. After Terry Newell, Randy Glenn and Peter Pepe had run we were abreast of Blackheath, a good 15 yards clear of the remainder. Although he had run a half-mile heat and final during the afternoon, John Thresher took last stage. He was obviously no match for Blackheath's Sampson, but could he hold off an impressive trio of runners who were pounding down on him from behind ? John was caught at the start of the long finishing straight, but showing tremendous fight and determination he held them off until the last two yards when the T.V.H. man got the verdict with a drop finish. Our final collections were one 4th, one 5th and two 6ths. Gerry Leroy was late for the start of the 220 yards final and had no time to use blocks. As a result, he was completely left at the gun; the man on his inside being level after 2 yards. Gerry made ground down the final straight but had to be content with 4th in 22.8, 0.3 of a second behind the winner. Our field place went to John Thresher in the 880 yards final, yet he was only inches short of second place. In a blanket finish John was given 1:59.0 to the runner's-up 1:58.9 - by such margins are trophies decided! Our two single point donations came from a jaded looking John Davies in the 1500 metres (4 minutes 1.6) and from that all-round field event man, George Edwards, with a 9'6" pole-vault. The spirit in which the various events were contested, and the support the various clubs received, were reminicent of earlier days. More enthusiasm abounded at this meeting than all the other trophy meetings put together. Perhaps it was because there was a lack of certain notable stars. This left the majority of events wide open and allowed a more friendly type of rivalry to prevail. Pos Club Points 1. T.V.H. 51 points. 2. Blackheath 45 " 3. Cambridge 44 " 4. H.H.H. 43 " 5. items.sum: Report of the 1961 Kinnaird Trophy at Chiswick on 10 June, notable for Malcolm Robinson's mile win, with Belgrave finishing joint last.
items.s: Kinnaird trophy : Report of the 1961 Kinnaird Trophy at Chiswick on 10 June, notable for Malcolm Robinson's mile win, with Belgrave finishing joint last. Highlight of this year's meeting, held at Chiswick on June 10th, was Malcolm Robinson's excellent mile win. Although he won in the relatively slow time of 4:16.0, it was a perfectly judged race and produced a last lap of 58 seconds. Bill Kerr, racing for the first time since his injury, ran a fine 14:14.6 three miles to finish 4th, but the remainder of our team, apart from Peter Eldridge, either failed to qualify for their finals or were outside the first six. Trevor Tolson ran in the 100 yards, Dave Carter the 220, Alan Jackson and John Thresher the 880, and Clive Shippen the steeplechase. Peter Eldridge was one of two athletes to suffer at the hands of a poor starter in the 440 yards final, and although well down at the start still managed to finish 3rd. Nothing of note was produced in the field events and as far as the team result was concerned this was one of our worst showings ever - finishing joint last with S.L.H. items.s: THE 1961 CHAMPIONSHIPS Ron Linstead's report of the 1961 Club Track and Field Championships at Hurlingham Park, with full senior, junior and boys' results (continued on page 26; the 880 winning time is 1:58.6 in the text and 1:58.8 in the table, and the boys 100 winner is R. Bevan in the text but J. Bevan in the table). RON LINSTEAD reports : Run in cold and very windy conditions this year's meeting, held at Hurlingham Park, was rather disappointing. The stands were almost empty and our stars of yesteryear conspicuous by their absence. Surely on this one particular day everyone should make an effort to attend. The childrens' races were even cancelled, due to lack of support - perhaps we have lost our virility as well as our cross-country titles! Star of the show was undoubtedly Gerry Leroy, who had four easy wins. His performance in the 440 yards was especially praiseworthy, coming as it did near the end of the programme. It was a pity there was no one capable of pushing Gerry, as he would certainly have gone even faster than the 49.4 he was credited. Randy Glenn, Terry Newell and Alan Jackson produced a blanket finish for 2nd, 3rd and 4th, all recording 51.5. The hardest fought race of the day was the Senior 880 yards. Alan Black was the early leader but 220 yards out Jackson, Thresher and Glenn swept by to each lead in turn down the long finishing straight before Jackson forged ahead once more in the closing stages to record 1: 58.6 - his future is indeed bright. Thresher, whose studies have made his training schedule one of the lightest in the club, was second in 1: 59.2 and the powerfully built Randy Glenn third in 1: 59.4 - his fastest time. A cloudburst and gale-force winds greeted the start of the Senior mile and made conditions even worse. As if this wasn't enough there had to be a false start! For two laps the holder, Malcolm Robinson, led the field through the elements until Don Maclean took over with Pat Newell and John Davies on his heels. With 300 yards to go these three were clear and Mac & Pat made their efforts with John hanging on grimly. A superb fighting effort by Davies on the last bend brought him back into contact with the leaders, and down the straight his superior speed took him to a well deserved victory in 4 : 26.0, having run the last two laps in 2 : 8.0. Mac, of late a much more consistent runner than he has been for several years, was second only a fifth of a second down, and Pat third in 4 : 27.6. Robinson was an unhappy fourth with a time some 20 seconds outside his best. The 2 miles walk resulted in an easy win for George Williams with 15 minutes 9 seconds. Much of the interest in this event was lost owing to the absence of Vickers, Hall and Middleton. The most impressive of the Juniors was David Cocks who took the 440 (53.1) and 880 (2:02.2) in magnificently relaxed style. His low, smooth, economical leg action makes it all look so easy. In the Boys events, strongly built Roger Hudson broke the 100 yards record in his heat with a time of 11.2. In the final, however, he was forced to give way to the other heat winner, R. Bevan, who clocked 11.3. Roger, primarily a quartermiler, made amends for this set back when he took the 880 yards in 2:09.5. Had he shown some restraint over the first lap - he went through in 59.0! - he might well have done about 2:04. The performances of our Boys, Youths and Juniors certainly indicated that, with continued careful coaching, we have some bright prospects in the making. Pos Name Perf 1. G. Leroy 10.3 2. P. items.sum: Account, quoting the Isle of Man Daily Times, of Ron Linstead's record-breaking win in the Isle of Man T.T. course road race on 22 May 1961, with the result and a note of other Belgrave road performances.
items.s: ROAD RUNNING Account, quoting the Isle of Man Daily Times, of Ron Linstead's record-breaking win in the Isle of Man T.T. course road race on 22 May 1961, with the result and a note of other Belgrave road performances. One of the outstanding performances this summer has been Ron Linstead's record-breaking win in the Isle of Man Road Race, held over the 37¾ mile T.T. course on May 22nd. But let the front page of the Isle of Man DAILY TIMES tell you the story with the following abbreviated extract:- "Records tumbled in yesterday's T.T. course road race. The first three men home were all inside the 3 hours 57 minutes 5 seconds target set by Tom Richards in 1956. And the new lap record holder, Ron Linstead (Belgrave Harriers) smashed the previous best by 6 minutes 25 seconds!.... (he) was home 4 minutes 15 seconds ahead of the second man, last year's winner, Don Turner (Epsom and Ewell Harriers)........ "Linstead, ....... had his first look at the course on Sunday when the runners were taken on a coach trip of the T.T. circuit. He was one of 13 newcomers in a field of 33....... But if he was unfamiliar with the circuit he was unafraid of the T.T. course's reputation. For at the first check point - the five mile mark - Linstead shared second place with E. Elderfield (T.V.H.) half a minute down on the leader, K. Heaton (Clayton-le-Moors)". "By the ten mile mark at the top of Creg Willys Hill, Linstead had taken the lead that he was to hold right to the end. But matching him stride for stride was Elderfield. They had opened a two minute gap, covering the ten miles in 63 minutes 2 seconds....... The 15 mile check point saw Linstead and Elderfield still running easily side by side, with a slightly increased lead. They passed the timekeepers in 1 hour 32 minutes 23 seconds. Watt & Smith were through in 1 : 34 : 36, then came Turner (1 : 34 : 38) and Lucop (1 : 34 : 49).......". "With 20 miles gone the leaders, Linstead and Elderfield, passed Kerrowmoor in 2 : 02 : 25. They had lost ground slightly to Watt and Smith, through in 2 : 03 : 44. But, significantly, the leading pair had stepped up their pace. They covered the second ten miles 4 minutes faster than the first 10. This was the first hint of the records to come. "At Kerrowmoor Turner held 5th place in 2 : 04 : 04 and sixth was H.W. Dennis (T.V.H.) in 2 : 06 : 15........". "The leaders were "clocked" at almost exactly 10 m.p.h. for their fourth 5 mile stint, and the record began to look in danger. Through Parliament Square Linstead headed Elderfield by several yards, and although he took the wrong turning - heading up Brookefield Avenue for a round of golf! - spectators turned him back to his correct path before he lost his lead. The lanky Elderfield was beginning to look tired now." "And Linstead passed the 25 mile post on his own, in 2 : 31 : 30. He had 17 seconds in hand over Elderfield, who was blowing painfully......into sixth place had moved B.C. Sawyer (Belgrave Harriers) with 2 : 37 : 15. It now seemed that Linstead must win. He was running easily up the mountain with no sign of strain. His partner of 15 gruelling miles, E. Elderfield, was not however faring so well, and the killing climb from the Gooseneck forced him to walk, while rival after rival edged past." "Linstead had a three minute lead with just 7¾ miles to go and the mountain climb behind him. Last year's winner, Turner, still had hopes of catching him, however, and called to the timekeepers for Linstead's lead. As the leader rounded Creg-ny-baa there was still no sign of Turner.........and the only question that remained was, could he break the record." "Yes, indeed he could. Ron Linstead crossed the line 3 hours, 50 minutes, 40 seconds after starting, to record his first big win in long distance road racing. After 37¾ miles Ron was not even breathing hard. His comment on the course - "The mountain is the only thing. I had a good race"." Apart from Linstead bouquets this season go to Gebbett for his excellent 4th place in the Wigmore '15' (1:22:26); to Sawyer - whose thirst for distance racing must make him our most travelled athlete; to the much improved Dennis Jones for his 6th place in the Kent '20' (1 : 55 : 44) and his 9th in the Chichester to Portsmouth '16' (1 : 33 : 45); and to Norman Stairs, who runs only in the summer, for his winning of the "A. items.label: July 1961
items.h: AROUND THE COUNTIES........ AND THE AREAS
items.sum: Round-up of Belgrave athletes at the 1961 county championships (Surrey, Middlesex, Bedfordshire, Yorkshire, Sussex) and area championships (Southern, Northern, Midland, Scottish).
items.s: AROUND THE COUNTIES........ AND THE AREAS Round-up of Belgrave athletes at the 1961 county championships (Surrey, Middlesex, Bedfordshire, Yorkshire, Sussex) and area championships (Southern, Northern, Midland, Scottish). SURREY Ray Middleton proved that long distance training does not necessarily blunt the speed for shorter races when winning the 2-miles walk title. He equalled his previous best time with 14 : 29 : 8, with the deposed holder, George Williams, in second place (14:34:4). Other runners-up for Belgrave were Gerry Leroy, 49.0 seconds 440 yards and Mal Robinson, 4 : 20 : 4 mile - after passing through the ½ mile in 2:17! Fifth in this latter event was John Thresher (4:26:0). In the qualifying heats of the 3 miles, held two days earlier, competitors had to achieve 15 minutes to qualify for the final. Don Maclean and Clive Shippen reached the final (Clive 15:00 exactly!), but Arthur Bruce 15:06) just failed to make it. Unfortunately, both our qualifiers produced slower times in the final and were way down the field. Alan Black (mile) and Pete Mitchell (880) were eliminated in their heats. MIDDLESEX At one time we used to have a healthy number of entries for this County's championships, but this year we had but one competitor, Pat Newell. However, Pat carried our colours high and gained a most worthy third place. His official time of 14.00 minutes exactly was given on a running watch! Several other watches placed him inside the 14.00 minute "barrier" - a tenth of a second here can mean a great deal to an athlete. Pat's effort was nearly 15 seconds faster than his previous best. BEDFORDSHIRE Peter Eldridge pulled off the treble once again. His times this year were, 100 yards - 9.9 seconds (equals Club record), 220 yards - 21.9 seconds, and 440 yards - 49.8 seconds. Great running from one of the best athletes we have ever had. YORKSHIRE. Once again Trevor Tolson annexed the 120 yards hurdles title. Despite a troublesome head wind he recorded 16.2 seconds. SUSSEX. Brian Morris finished first in the final of the 220 yards with 22.6 seconds, and later came out to make it a double by retaining his 440 yards title with a winning time of 49.4 seconds. ........AND THE AREAS SOUTHERN There were too few Belgravians competing in this year's championship, held at Motspur Park. The number of "claret and gold" vests seems to dwindle year by year. Of those members who competed on this hottest day of the year, pride of place must go to Brian Morris who was 4th in the 440 yards. Halfway down the final straight he was seemingly doomed for sixth place, but a superhuman effort took him past two rivals to record 48.3 seconds - an excellent time. Gerry Leroy, not quite at his best this season, was eliminated in the semi-finals. Mal Robinson failed to qualify for the star-studded mile final, finishing sixth in his heat with 4 minutes 12.8! No one envied Pat Newell, who ran in the 3 miles main event. For besides the oppresive heat he also had to contend with Messrs. Pirie, Hyman, Eldon & Co. Pat ran, relatively, as well as anybody in the field to record 14:14, but was outside the first six. Alan Black & Clive Shippen ran in the 3,000 meters steeplechase, but both showed poor form, Alan recording 9:51 and Clive just outside 10 minutes. NORTHERN Trevor Tolson hurdled beautifully to record 15.2 seconds in the 120 yards high hurdles and finish second behind international R. Birrell. Trevor, who first gained an A.A.A. vest 10 years ago, says he will keep at it until he breaks that magical 15 seconds. Incidentally, his time of 15.2 sets a new club record - improving by one-fifth of a second on Mal Ash's mark set in 1955. MIDLAND The ever-reliable Peter Eldridge was another to do credit to the name of BELGRAVE. He finished an excellent third in the 220 yards final behind Peter Radford and Robbie Brightwell, recording 22.4 seconds. Peter followed this up in the 440 yards final by recording 48.2 in second place behind Barry Jackson, another International. SCOTTISH Travelling to his homeland in an endeavour to record times to qualify for the A.A.A. championships, Bill Kerr unwisely ran in the six-mile event on the Friday evening. After passing the halfway mark in 14:32 he was obliged to drop out. The following day, in a slow-run race, he was placed third in the 3 miles with 14:31:2, being beaten for speed at the end. Don Maclean (with a name like that I suppose he must be Scottish!) was also running at the Championships. Don also claims Welsh qualifications and had their meeting not been on the same day as the Southern he would have run their too! Anyway, this cosmopolitan character finished fifth in the mile event with 4:25. items.label: January 1962
items.sum: New Year editorial stressing individual training, announcing Dave Mitchell as co-editor in place of Malcolm Robinson (now at the University of Southern Louisiana), welcoming Gerry North, and thanking Arthur Bruce and Ed Lacey.
items.s: EDITORIAL New Year editorial stressing individual training, announcing Dave Mitchell as co-editor in place of Malcolm Robinson (now at the University of Southern Louisiana), welcoming Gerry North, and thanking Arthur Bruce and Ed Lacey. May we wish you all the very best of health and success in 1962. We could express the usual wishes about a renewal of the Belgrave athletic fortunes but we prefer to emphasise the importance of individual effort within the framework of the Club. If we can find that essential nucleus of champions then assuredly team results will also improve and major championship successes follow. Let us all bear in mind that actions speak far louder than words and the basis of all good athletic performances is TRAINING. Since our last issue there has been a change in the Editorship. Dave Mitchell has succeeded Malcolm Robinson who recently gained a scholarship at the University of Southern Louisiana, U.S.A. — we wish him the greatest success both athletically and scholastically. We should like to take this opportunity of welcoming into the Club the many members who have joined us since our last issue — in particular Gerry North. Gerry will be moving to the Wimbledon area in February and if any of our readers know of any furnished flats suitable for him and his wife we, the Editors, shall be pleased to hear from them. We congratulate Gerry on his excellent win in the Inter-Counties Championship and hope he will have many similar successes in Belgrave colours. Our thanks are extended to Arthur Bruce for the excellent cartoons we include in this issue, and also to Ed Lacey for his many photographs. items.label: January 1962
items.sum: Obituary of Dick Savage, a member for fifty years, former President, runner, official, R.W.A. judge and donor of the Savage Shield, by A.A. Harley.
items.s: R. J. SAVAGE Obituary of Dick Savage, a member for fifty years, former President, runner, official, R.W.A. judge and donor of the Savage Shield, by A.A. Harley. It is with very profound regret that we have to advise the death of Dick Savage, and our sincere sympathy is extended to Mrs. Savage and other members of the family. We shall miss him tremendously; and also the work and enthusiasm he contributed in such ample measure over so many years to the Belgrave Harriers. It is fifty years since Dick joined the Club as a young man in his early twenties and immediately he made his contribution to the Club, both as a runner and an official. His membership of Prices A.C. helped to forge links with the Belgrave Harriers which were mutually beneficial for very many years. After the First World War, Dick was one of the first, with Bob Ricketts, Jimmy Belchamber, Harry Parker, Oscar Horwood, Harry Evans and others, to start re-building the Club. It was hard work indeed at first; but before long the results began to show, and with the acquisition of new members such as Harry Hare (who was a most efficient Hon. Secretary & Treasurer within twelve months of joining the Club, and Hon. Editor of our first printed Gazette) and stabilisation of our Winter Headquarters at Wimbledon, Belgrave began to forge ahead. Dick played his effective, though unobtrusive, part within the Club's progress, and was always available and always willing to help in any way possible. Thus the writer remembers him as pointsman, slow-pack leader, doorman at our Dances and Socials - always present, always helpful. In later years he became a respected President of the Club, a most efficient Timekeeper, an R.W.A. Judge, and presented us with the "SAVAGE" Shield for Junior Cross-country Competition. In several years, he served as Junior Captain, placing his experience and knowledge at the disposal of the younger members, doing work which was of the utmost value. For fifty years Belgrave was a major part of his life, as indeed it has been of Mrs. Savage, who accompanied her husband whenever possible. In recent years, he had played the part of "Father Christmas" at our Childrens Party; which seemed to give added point to those virtues of loyalty, gentleness, kindliness, good-humour and generosity with which we associated Dick as one of Nature's Gentlemen. We owe him a great debt we can never repay; and we are grateful indeed for his fifty years of ever-helpful membership. A.A.HARLEY. R.J. (Dick) Savage Dick Savage Dick Savage R. J. items.label: January 1962
items.sum: Ernie Duffett's Club Dinner speech introducing new President Arthur Penny, recounting his cross-country and track career of the late 1920s and 1930s.
items.s: THE PRESIDENT Ernie Duffett's Club Dinner speech introducing new President Arthur Penny, recounting his cross-country and track career of the late 1920s and 1930s. In introducing Arthur Penny as Club President we here print the speech made by Ernie Duffett at this year's Club Dinner. "Arthur Penny joined the Club in February, 1928 and was known as 'Nutty' in those days, the reason being obvious when you gaze on his shining bald pate. He soon made his mark and was placed 3rd in the Surrey County C.C. Championships in 1929, with myself 4th, Bill Mitchell 5th and we had our scoring 6 in the first 15 to finish. We thus took the team title from South London H. and actually won this championship 8 times out of 9 years and Arthur was our key man in most of these victories. He was also a member of our winning South of Thames 'Senior' team in 1929, and won the individual title in the Surrey C.C. Championship in 1931, also the 1933 Southern Counties C.C. Championship, which was won by Bert Footer. In those days it was impossible to see the name of Penny without that of Footer being close alongside, and they became known as the 'Belgrave Twins' and Laurie Richardson, who was then the Secretary of the English C.C. Union had a very high opinion of their capabilities. They finished 4th and 5th in the National C.C. race at Alderley Edge in 1933, in what Arthur has described as his most thrilling race. Arthur also finished 5th in the 1934 National, and was 2nd in the Southern Counties C.C. at Taplow, where Belgrave won the team title for the first time. In the International C.C. race at Ayr in 1934 Arthur was placed 3rd with Bert Footer 4th, and they helped England to an easy victory in the team championship. I think that Arthur and Bert were the first to start the 7-day week training routine which is now commonplace, but in those days most athletes were content with a run on Tuesday and Thursday evenings and then Saturday afternoon. Arthur was also a member of our winning London to Brighton Road Relay teams, which was then the National race only, which scored a triumphant hat-trick of wins in 1934, 1935 and 1936, a feat never before accomplished. They were great days for Belgrave and we were almost invincible over road and country, and it was quoted by a well-known economist that 'The sterling qualities of the Belgrave Harriers are clearly based on the right use of the Penny.' Arthur was made a Life Member of the Club in 1934, and then was out of athletics for the whole of the 1935 season due to a fractured bone in his foot. He was back to form in 1936, however, when he again won the Surrey County C.C. championship and also led our team to victory in the team race. He just missed selection for the 1936 Olympic Games, and in 1937 was placed 4th with Pat Parker 3rd, Bert Footer 6th, Tom Carter 7th, Les Cohen 15th and Alf Taylor 16th in the Union Sportive C.C. race near Paris, in which Belgrave won the team race, beating all the leading French and Belgian clubs, and they appeared on television under the Baird process, after which it was agreed by the powers that be, to use the E.M.I. process. Arthur was also a great man in 2 and 3 miles team races, on the track, and his crowning glory was when he won the Empire Games 6 miles track title in 1934 at White City, London. He also won the Club 3 miles track title many times and from the number of times he won the "Blackstaffe" Shield for the Club 7 miles C.C. Championships, he almost made it a permanent possession on his sideboard. I also remember when he won a Club half-mile handicap off 65 yards and then later he won the Boxing Day 2 miles run off the scratch mark, which takes some doing. Arthur was a very useful runner at all distances, and in 1938 was placed 3rd in the A.A.A. 10 miles track championship. I understand that we have some useful youngsters coming along, and if they will only set their sights on the heights attained by Arthur Penny, then we can ask no more of them. I ask you to be upstanding and drink the health of our President, Arthur Penny." items.label: January 1962
items.sum: New Year message from President A.W.C. Penny in the club's 75th year, with sympathy to Mrs. Savage.
items.s: A message from your PRESIDENT : New Year message from President A.W.C. Penny in the club's 75th year, with sympathy to Mrs. Savage. Dear Belgravians, It is with pride and pleasure that I write to you as your President in the 75th year of the Club's existence. Much has been achieved in that time. There is no need for me to enlarge on our successes or our failings, sufficient is it for me to say that if we all strive to do our best, Belgrave once again can reach the top. In conclusion, I know you will all join with me in offering our deepest sympathy with Mrs. Savage in her sorrow at the passing of her husband Dick. Wishing you all success in the coming year. items.s: 3 MILES TRACK CHAMPIONSHIP Report and result of the 1961 club 3 miles track championship, retained by Mal Robinson in the absence of many leading runners. Kerr, Newell, Davies, Walker, Black, Dabbs, Linstead, Maclean. How's that for a line up to set a new 3 mile record? Yet these were all the names that did not run. Each no doubt, had excellent reasons for missing this Club Championship, but their absence only helped to boost the ego of the holder, Mal Robinson, who must be forgiven for feeling like the heavyweight boxing champion whom no-one wished to meet. Mal showed that he too can be unsociable, and after one lap decided to retain his title without company. This was an uncharacteristic move, but despite a very strong head-wind in the back straight, it paid dividends. Jack Brown, who has won this trophy on four consecutive occasions, made every effort to close the gap, but halving it was the most he could manage and so had to be content with second place. Barry Sawyer moved through the field after a mile and had little difficulty in gaining third place, while Dick Shackleford - always to the fore - finished fourth. New member Laurie O'Hara, principally a footballer, ran very well in his first "three" to finish a surprise fifth. Little can be said of the remainder. Bruce and Shippen were lethargic and Lennie Bishop faded after a promising start; but young Alan Morrison should feel encouraged, performing as he did in this his first race over the distance. items.s: 6 MILES TRACK CHAMPIONSHIP: Robinson's last lap sees him through! Report and result of the 1961 club 6 miles track championship, won by Malcolm Robinson in his last race before leaving for America. Held on a somewhat cold and blustery evening, this, the last of the club track championships for 1961, was unfortunately made notable by the absence of several prospective champions. After three somewhat abortive laps by Clive Shippen, Malcolm Robinson was in no mood for pleasantries and proceeded to 'sit in' content in the knowledge that his was the faster finish. In the earlier stages Charlie Walker remained in close contact with the two leaders but gradually he was made to yield ground and left to make certain of third place. Some five hundred yards from home Malcolm left Jackie dis-spirited by his enforced role as leader, tip-toed round a final lap of 62 secs. and finished some 70 yrds to the good. items.label: January 1962
items.sum: D.E.M.'s review of a disappointing 1961 track season, highlighting the A.A.A. 4 x 440 yards relay second place and club record, Brian Morris, Peter Eldridge, Bill Kerr's records, John Thresher and the departing Mal Robinson.
items.s: TRACK ROUND-UP D.E.M.'s review of a disappointing 1961 track season, highlighting the A.A.A. 4 x 440 yards relay second place and club record, Brian Morris, Peter Eldridge, Bill Kerr's records, John Thresher and the departing Mal Robinson. To be frank, this has in most respects been a disappointing season. There have been too few individual and team successes. Certainly the track reputation of the Club has been enhanced almost solely by the performances of our quarter-milers whereas the field events section has been most notable by its virtual absence. Pride of place must surely be given to the four Belgrave boys, Peter Eldridge, Brian Morris, Graham Worrall, and Gerry Leroy, who gained second place in the A.A.A's 4 x 440 yds relay. Faced with a Birchfield quartet of international calibre our lads proved themselves to be a most powerful and courageous combination. They finished in a time of 3:15.3, only 2.1 seconds behind the Midland club, broke the existing A.A.A's record, and established a new Club and Southern Counties best performance. We must also pay tribute to Messrs. Gordon, Thresher, Pepe, and Leroy for their excellent second place in the Surrey County Championships on July 29th. "Evergreen" Gordon battled round the first lap to put us well in the hunt, John kept the pressure on, Pete put us into the places, and Gerry pulled out a 48.6 last lap to put us exactly two seconds behind the Hercules team who broke the existing record set in 1959 by a Belgrave team. Brian Morris finally established himself as our fastest one lap man of the season by returning 48.0 in the L.C.C. Championships at Hurlingham early in September. As usual Brian ran an 'easy' first 300 yards and in fact only just 'got up' to pip Poly's Mike Potter on the post. If only Brian's pace over the first couple of hundred yards was a little hotter he would almost certainly be down among the 47 second men. How about it then Brian? Peter Eldridge has again proved himself a versatile, consistent, and capable performer. Once more he completed the sprint hat-trick in the Bedforshire Championships and has had several representative runs throughout the season, won an invitation furlong at the White City, finished second in the London v Rhineland inter-cities quarter at the same venue. Apart from the quarter-milers and our now flourishing Juniors, there have been few memorable performances or performers. One successful athlete, however, has been a newcomer from north of the border. Bill Kerr has proved himself a popular character, a fine athlete, and a valuable Club member. He established a new club record of 8:55 for two miles in the London Clubs race, and capped a season of fine running by finishing a good second to T.V.H. International Haith in the Melbourne Trophy 3,000 m. at Tooting. He beat several established stars to clock 8:21, a new club best performance. John Thresher ran several courageous races for the Club, his determination compensating in some measure for his comparative lack of training. His 1:55.0 half-mile placed him second on the club list to Bob Norton for the 1961 season. Finally some mention must be made of Mal Robinson. His departure to America for a college course will leave us quite considerably the poorer. Impetuous and outspoken he may have been, but his loyalty and enthusiasm were undoubted. Two club track championships became his during the season and his winning of the Kinnaird Trophy mile was a little masterpiece of timing and confident determination. If Mal's spirit were more prevalent throughout Belgrave we would once again be winning the championships and trophies. We wish him all the very best and hope that we shall not have to refer to him in the past tense for too long. D.E.M. D.E.M. D.E.M. items.s: ROAD - RELAYS: Surrey Co. Road Relay : Report and result of the Surrey County Road Relay at Woking Lido on 9 September 1961, where Belgrave finished sixth and S.L.H. won with Gordon Pirie fastest. Held on September 9th from that most pleasant venue, the Woking Lido, this year's event was a repeat of our un-pleasant performances of recent years. The usual difficulty was experienced in raising a team which, when formed, had the usual un-fit look about it. Perhaps the "Brighton" wasn't yet close enough! For five stages we hovered in 7th and 8th positions until Alan Black squeezed us into a more respectable 6th place on the final leg. This was Gordon Pirie's last road relay for S.L.H. (the winners) and his final solo run was only 4 secs. outside the course record he set 8 years earlier! Pos Team Time 1. S.L.H. 84:13.4 2. H.H.H. 86:20.8 3. Hercules A.C. 87:27.8 4. items.h: GREAT RUN BY KERR IN POLYTECHNIC'S RELAY
items.sum: Report and result of the Polytechnic Relay at Chiswick on 16 September 1961 (8 x 3 miles), where Bill Kerr's last leg lifted Belgrave to second.
items.s: GREAT RUN BY KERR IN POLYTECHNIC'S RELAY Report and result of the Polytechnic Relay at Chiswick on 16 September 1961 (8 x 3 miles), where Bill Kerr's last leg lifted Belgrave to second. CHISWICK Sept. 16th (8 x 3mls) A sensational last-leg stint by Bill Kerr lifted Belgrave into a noteworthy second place, just two secs. ahead of rivals, T.V.H. Amid intense excitement, Bill set off in 4th place 18 secs. behind Herne Hill and a full half minute behind the Valley, and after what must have been the fastest 2 mls. ever run on this course had passed both his rivals! With half a mile to go he was a good 20yds clear, but the fireworks were by no means over, for Saunders of T.V.H. put in a desperate effort to close the gap on the tiring figure ahead. Inch by inch he moved up, until with 100 yds to go, they were level. Accompanied by the frenzied shouts of their supporters, the two runners raced for the line, but Bill proved too strong for the gallant Valley man and in clocking 13:02, became the second fastest runner of the day. Forty three teams started in this popular event, and Belgrave fielded four of them. Eric Gebbett ran his usual reliable first stage, keeping us in contact with the leaders and Charlie Walker consolidated this by moving us up to 3rd position. On the third leg, Jack Brown maintained our place with an excellent 13:36, and although he was the "A" team's slowest man, John Thresher (14:09) ran well enough to take us up to second, 43 secs. behind the eventual winners - Polytechnic Harriers. John Davies, Ron Linstead and Alan Black ran the next three stages all within 15 secs. of each other, and although we dropped two places we were still within striking distance of second place - as Bill Kerr showed only too well! Our "B", "C", and "D" teams also produced some good performances notably from Maclean, Sawyer and Forey, and all but the "C" team closed in. An excellent turn-out. "C" & "D" Teams. D. W. items.s: KERR WINS 5¾ ROAD RACE Report and result of the club 5¾ miles road race used to assess form for the Brighton Relay, won by Bill Kerr, with the handicap won by A. Penstone. Used for assessing form for the forthcoming Brighton Relay, this race was held on a heavy sultry day, not conducive to good running. The whole race was run in a lethargic manner and it was soon obvious that, barring accident, Bill Kerr would be the winner. Jack Brown made a valiant effort to keep the gap as small as possible between himself and the loping Scot ahead, but Bill seemed to have the matter well in hand at all times. The early part of the race had seen the field well bunched for the first lap of the Common, but down Copse Hill, the leaders were strung out with Kerr, Brown, Gebbett, Walker and Sawyer prominent. Linstead took a steady start which in the end paid dividends, for he moved through to third position. Lower down the field John Davies and Cyril Forey were running together - the former running within his obvious capabilities, the latter short of training and feeling his way carefully. It was good to see John Moore back in club races, we need his help and hope he can regain his position of a year or two ago. The final times were disappointingly slow, probably due to the weather, but it was pleasing to see the leaders fairly well bunched. Handicap - 1. A.Penstone 27:41.2 B. Members are reminded that current subscriptions became due on September 1st. Those members still in arrears are asked to honour their obligations by sending their remittances to the Hon. Treasurer himself or contacting the three assistant Hon. Treasurers - Messrs. Morrell, Dewsbury, and Cornelius, who are present at most Club activities. * * * * * Eric Gebbett has now moved house to Leighton Buzzard, but assures us he will remain first-claim Belgrave. His loyalty is much appreciated and is in keeping with the stalwart support he has given Belgrave teams for many a year. Congratulations Eric on the second addition to your family. We are relieved to hear that both your son and daughter have inherited their mother's feet! * * * * * We also extend congratulation to Jill and Len Bishop on the birth of their daughter Angela. Eric Bishop won this particular race several years ago with his son Clive and it now only remains for brother Alan to close in for Bishop Harriers! items.h: SOUTHERN LONDON-BRIGHTON RELAY: DISAPPOINTING 6th BY BELGRAVE
items.sum: 'Olympian's stage-by-stage report of Belgrave's sixth place in the 1961 Southern London to Brighton Relay, with the top-ten result and photographs of Jack Brown handing over to Bill Kerr and Cyril Forey taking over from Clive Shippen (continued on page 10).
items.s: SOUTHERN LONDON-BRIGHTON RELAY: DISAPPOINTING 6th BY BELGRAVE 'Olympian's stage-by-stage report of Belgrave's sixth place in the 1961 Southern London to Brighton Relay, with the top-ten result and photographs of Jack Brown handing over to Bill Kerr and Cyril Forey taking over from Clive Shippen (continued on page 10). Our performance in the National Relay in April when we finished fifth, encouraged us to think we would be amongst the honours for this event, which is limited only to Southern clubs. On paper our team appeared to be strong enough to give even Portsmouth a run for their money, but we were to be disappointed. Our confidence proved to be ill-founded and we were to finish no higher than sixth. The usual crop of scares during the week before the race kept the selection committee on tenterhooks but in the end the team that turned out was almost up to full strength. The day of the race dawned fine and clear and the team manager at Westminster thought he would have little or nothing to worry about. Two runners and a reserve are instructed to report to Great Smith Street Baths at 9.00a.m. for the 10.o'clock start. One of the runners and the reserve duly appeared, but the second leg runner was missing, and the minutes ticked by without a sign of the absent Belgravian. The team manager's fingernails got shorter and shorter and his nerves more and more frayed. The anxious reserve was duly despatched to Clapham Common and the race was started without news of Pat Newell. STAGE I - Alan Black ( 21:14. 7th fastest) Alan set off along the Embankment not knowing to whom he would pass his baton. This may have had some effect on his running for he could do no better than seventh, 26 secs. behind Harvey of Mitcham who gave his Club a perfect start. Alan has run well to Queens Circus but seemed to lose his grip on the race over the next half mile; a set-back from which he did not recover. STAGE II - Pat Newell ( 25:18. 3rd fastest) On arrival at Clapham Common we were delighted to find Pat Newell on his mark, but it would have saved many problems if instructions had been carried out, or a 'phone call made to Bill Lucas. Pat set off in grand style and soon closed the gap on the teams ahead, with the exception of Portsmouth, who moved quickly into the lead with an excellent run by B. Cooke. Haith of T.V.H. caught and passed Newell by the time Tooting Bec Station was reached, but Pat kept his head and in the end took us up to third position, 36 secs, behind the leaders; an excellent effort. STAGE 3 - Ron Linstead (29:47. 9th) Ron was soon passed by Richards of Polytechnic, but hung on gamely and at the beginning of Purley Way was still in 4th place, although losing ground on the leaders. Lewis of Woodford, running at his best, and Perkins of Ilford were making great progress from behind and up the long slope past Croydon Airport forced Ron to concede further places. At Purley Ron overtook Stacey of T.V.H. and we were fifth at the change-over, 77secs. behind Portsmouth who had consolidated their lead and were never again to be headed. STAGE 4 - Barry Sawyer (26:15. 8th) This stage had been given to one of our most improved runners who was performing in a "Brighton" for the first time. Barry runs immense distances in training and is a very fit man, but lacks the necessary speed at the moment for good relay running: it is possible that a day's rest from the hard daily grind before a race such as this would produce a little more snap. Nevertheless Barry ran well and although losing two places to Mitcham and T.V.H. had established himself and will without doubt earn many more team selections. STAGE 5 - Eric Gebbett (22:36. 8th) Always prepared to run on whichever leg he is most needed, Eric was unfortunate enough to set off through Redhill with a gap of 45 secs. between himself and the runner ahead. This was not the ideal set-up for Eric, he runs at his best when in close contact, and in consequence we did not benefit from Eric's considerable experience as we had hoped. Eric reached Earl's Wood still in 6th place and nearer to the fifth team, but was nearly three minute behind Portsmouth who were increasing their lead on every leg. STAGE 6 - John Davies (13:59 4th ) John did not produce the performance of which we all know he is capable. In the past year or so he has seemed afraid to really let himself go. He puts in many training sessions and with a 4:10 mile as a basis should be one of our fastest runners over distances up to four miles. This leg is the shortest of all and is generally given to the weaker members of each team, so although he produced the fourth best time today, and gained one place, his effort was still - to some of us - somewhat disappointing. STAGE 7 - Charlie Dabbs (19:06. 7th) Coming into the team as a result of the illness of John Thresher and an injury to Brian Hallowell, Chas. ran a steady leg across Gatwick Airport but was obviously still feeling the effects of his enforced layoff a few weeks earlier when he underwent a nasal operation. STAGE 8 - Jack Brown (31:50. 15th) Jack took over still in 6th place but 3½ mins. behind Portsmouth. Jack was obviously not at his best, and although plugging along on what is the hardest stage of all, was noticeably losing ground on all teams ahead. We have become accustomed to take for granted the fine performances of this experienced runner, but his run on this occasion gave us the final proof that this was not to be our day. At Handcross we were over five minutes behind. STAGE 9 - Bill Kerr ( 30:16. 12th fastest) Once again on the leg over which he had run so well in April, Bill could not reproduce similar form and we were destined to fall even further behind, although keeping in 6th place. Bill had been suffering with a slight leg injury during the previous week and this may well have had a bad effect on his running, combined with the sight of a road ahead bare of runners - not exactly the right incentive for a fast run. STAGE 10 - Charlie Walker (21:09. 5th fastest) Chas. gave a little on T.V.H. and Mitcham, but the gap was far too great to give the supporters any hope that we would finish higher than sixth. Charlie's effort was completely solo, T.V.H. being 2½ mins. ahead and Essex Beagles 1½ mins. behind! STAGE 11 - Clive Shippen (21:09. 4th fastest) Clive made further progress up Dale Hill and it was good to see our cross-country captain regaining the form he showed on this leg two years ago. Of the five teams ahead, we gained on Mitcham once more, and on Polytechnic, who were proving to be the surprise team of the day. STAGE 12 - Cyril Forey (17:50. 2nd fastest) Cyril set off on the last stage into Brighton with the gap ahead still over two minutes. He nevertheless put in an excellent run which gave him 2nd fastest time of the day and we arrived in Brighton in the 6th position we had held since the half-way mark. We have to do much better than this next April if we are to be amongst the leading teams. Perhaps we need some new blood in our teams. Heck, Miller, Thresher, Moore and Johnston are but a few knocking on the door to 1st team honours. There are also those up-and-coming lads Cocks, Hampshire and Fairclough who will be dis-placing a few old-timers before long. Pos Team Time 1. Portsmouth A.C. 4:31.56 2. Woodford Grn A.C. 4:36.28 3. items.sum: Report and result of the Chelmsford Road Relay on 28 October 1961, where Charlie Dabbs was summoned at short notice to complete the team, which finished fifth.
items.s: 'BELS.' AVOID EMBARRASSING SITUATION Report and result of the Chelmsford Road Relay on 28 October 1961, where Charlie Dabbs was summoned at short notice to complete the team, which finished fifth. CHELMSFORD ROAD RELAY (6 x 3⅓) October 28th. It was with a sigh of relief that our first five runners watched Charlie Dabbs set off on the last leg of this premier road relay. Not just because we were a well-placed second, but because three hours earlier, we fully expected to "run-out" after five stages - an embarrassing situation at the best of times, but when it is an "A" team lying second ahead of fifty other teams, then adverse comment and criticism is inevitable from all quarters. It was not until 10 mins before departure time from Liverpool St. Station that the team realised our sixth man would fail to appear. Hurriedly a phone-call was put through to Charlie Dabbs who, despite having trained already that morning, sportingly agreed to dash to Chelmsford for the last leg duty. Hence the team's sigh when Charlie set off in second position. It was not important that an off-form, psychologically unprepared and tired Dabbs dropped us to a final placing of 5th; we had closed in a team wearing Belgrave's colours. It was therefore with mixed feelings that we followed the gradual progress of our earlier runners. Eric Gebbett finished a well placed 8th, Clive Shippen moved up to 6th, Ron Linstead to 4th, and an excellent effort by Bill Kerr took us to 2nd, only 14 secs behind a strong Woodford team. Although losing ground to R. Bell, Cyril Forey maintained our place and thus it was that Charlie's unfortunate, but memorable run began. items.s: The Reigate Relay : Report and result of the Reigate cross-country relay, where Belgrave 'A' were fifth (the position figure in the result is overtyped) and Bill Kerr ran the fastest leg of the day (continued on page 12). Although Belgrave were destined for only 5th place in the team result, Bill Kerr enhanced his reputation by clocking fastest time of the day over this 2½ miles cross-country course. His excellent time of 9:45 was achieved on the third leg when taking his team from 7th to 2nd place. John Davies set a fast pace on the first stage, taking the field up a half-mile of steep hill, in good form, but faded somewhat in the middle stages. A good start, and a strong finish, however gave him the good time of 10:19 and Charlie Walker a line of nine runners all handily placed for "picking off". Charlie had been virtually out of training for 10 days due to a leg wound but his natural ability took him to a surprising 10:16 & Belgrave to 7th. After Bill's great effort had taken us to second, Clive Shippen was forced to give away two places and a very unfit Ken Miller another. Don Maclean took on the last leg run and easily held our fifth place. He has never been known to bound over the summit of a hill this size in such fine fettle! Of the "B" and "C" teams, Eric Penny and Fred Paget showed good form, and Alan Jackson's effort was most useful. items.sum: Report and result of the South of Thames Junior cross-country championship at Sevenoaks on 11 November 1961, where Belgrave took second team despite Barry Sawyer's enforced stop.
items.s: BELS. PLACED IN STH. of THAMES 'JUNIOR' EVENT Report and result of the South of Thames Junior cross-country championship at Sevenoaks on 11 November 1961, where Belgrave took second team despite Barry Sawyer's enforced stop. Sevenoaks — Nov 11th : This race will go down in Club History as the event in which Belgrave were 'bowelled' over and robbed of a title by purely natural causes. Barry Sawyer will remember this day for many a long year - he will never be allowed to forget it! Taking time out of a race, however short, usually precludes any chance of winning, and Barry's short sojourn into the bushes of Knowle Park meant the loss of some 150 places which even to a fit man like Barry presented an impossible task. His final placing of 42nd speaks for itself - from the time of his re-entry into the race he went through the field like a 'dose of salts' and eventually secured a second team medal by being our fourth scorer. Our leading runners got away to a good start and Alan Black and Barry Sawyer were prominent with Mike Heck not far behind and Clive Shippen backing up well. With misfortune overtaking Barry our position looked bad, for our next runner was outside the first hundred. At the half-way stage Alan was eleventh, Mike was just behind in fourteenth position and Clive was 33rd. By now Barry was recovering ground at a phenomenal rate but still appeared to be out of the picture. At the finish Alan had gained a little with his fast finish, Mike had fallen away slightly but Clive, by persistent running, had moved up to 22nd. Where would the fourth scorer finish? We knew Joe Dooley was making steady progress after his usual slow start. But the prospects of a position forward enough to give us a chance of a place were remote. To our surprise Barry was the next finisher and secured for us a total of 89 points and second team position. Without doubt we would have won if Barry had not been forced temporarily to retire. 80. items.label: January 1962
items.sum: Harry Shields' report of the 1961 Annual General Meeting, at which Arthur Penny succeeded Les Cohen as President and new officers were elected.
items.s: THE A.G.M. Harry Shields' report of the 1961 Annual General Meeting, at which Arthur Penny succeeded Les Cohen as President and new officers were elected. HARRY SHIELDS REPORTS. Another cycle of club life was marked by the A.G.M., when we were called to review our hopes and failures of the past 12 months to formulate our plans for the ensuing year, and to exercise our democratic privileges of criticising and electing Officers to whom we entrust the well-running of the Club. The nature of athletics is such that there is a large turnover of men entering and leaving the sport and although for stability it is essential to have the continuity of a number of grey-heads, it is even more important we delegate responsibility to younger members who have the necessary enthusiasm and interest of the sport at heart. At this year's meeting, we missed a number of the more voluble members from whom we have grown accustomed to learn our defects, but were amply compensated by a good gathering of youths and juniors, whose contribution to the discussions and willingness to join actively in the administration of the Club was a pleasing feature. Of the proceedings, we first had a report by the Hon. Secretary on the past year, from which we saw that our walkers still reigned supreme, the runners had many brilliant performances to their credit, but the field events men required strengthening and better leadership. The Hon. Treasurer's report showed we had little to fear financially. The election of Officers then proceeded and the retiring President Les Cohen, nominated as his successor, Arthur Penny, Empire Games Chamption English C.C. International, County Champion and stalwart of our pre-war track and cross-country teams. This was carried with acclaimation. Senior officers were elected with little change apart from Assistant Hon. Secretary F. Jarvis, Assistant Hon. Treasurer - P. J. Cornelius, Field Events Hon. Secretary - M. F. Jones, Social Hon. Secretary - T. Hart. Members were asked to give these officers every co-operation while they settled down in their jobs. Les Cohen was thanked for his work in connection with the Football Pontoon run by the Supporters Club, and the notice of members was drawn to the essential part this played in the welfare of the Club. The enthusiasm and improvements made by our Youths and Juniors brought forth comment and the work of J. Hampshire and T.C. Carter was praised. It was pleasing to see Ron Linstead and Dave Mitchell elected to shoulder the tasks of Press Hon. Secretary and Hon. Co. Editor of the 'Belgravian' respectively, and that the elected Committee comprised a balance of experience and youth. No controversial subjects were fought out and the meeting terminated with the feeling that progress had been made and the Club could look forward to a year of continued success. items.sum: Report of the 1961 club dinner at the Ardington Rooms, Clapham Junction, on 18 November, with speeches by E. Clynes, Harry Shields, Alf Harley, Ernie Duffet and President Arthur Penny.
items.s: THE CLUB DINNER - 1961 Report of the 1961 club dinner at the Ardington Rooms, Clapham Junction, on 18 November, with speeches by E. Clynes, Harry Shields, Alf Harley, Ernie Duffet and President Arthur Penny. Ladies seem to spend all day preparing for it, speakers are supposed to practise for hours in front of a mirror, and the day after usually means an overdose of aspirins and liver salts. What is it? Why the Belgrave annual dinner, of course! This year's function was held in the Ardington Rooms at Clapham Junction on November 18th, and as usual was made memorable by an overall atmosphere of warmth and fellowship. This keynote of friendship was initiated by our new club President, for Arthur and his wife were on the threshold, as it were, to welcome us into the fold. The after-dinner speeches were all quite brief and lively. Mr. E. Clynes, Secretary of the A.A.A, paid tribute to the great contribution our club has made to athletics. Harry Shields, with the help of Kipling and Shakespeare, made a most suitable response and managed to pull Bob Barnes's leg into the bargain. Alf Harley introduced and welcomed several guests in his accustomed informative manner - by the way, did you know that Harry Evans is now 80 years young and was invited as a guest to the dinner? Ernie Duffet stepped into a last minute breach and told us of the mammoth achievements of Arthur Penny in the '30's - I bet many youngsters were thinking, 'I didn't know he was that good'. Finally, Arthur paid tribute to his clubmates such as Bert 'Syrup of Figs' Footer, and expressed his pride in being honoured with this year's Presidency. After these somewhat informal formalities (!) dancing (and drinking of course) continued until half past eleven and Sid Roberts and the Social Committee were happy in the knowledge that a good time had been had by all. items.s: BELS. 2nd IN LONDON CHAMPS. Report and result of the London County cross-country championships at Parliament Hill Fields on 25 November 1961, where Belgrave were second to Highgate by three points. Parliament Hill Fields — Nov.25th: Running on their own territory Highgate Harriers won the London County C.C. championships for the fourth consecutive year, thus improving on Belgrave's run of victories in 1955,56 and 57. As usual, it was a very close contest - three points in fact, decided the issue. We stand a good chance of commencing another run of wins next year as the individual winner, Highgate's George Brown was running his last race in their colours before joining Welwyn A.C. Ron Linstead was first over the hill at the start, with the rest of the team close behind. It was not long, however, before Ron felt the effects of the rough going and steadily lost ground. Barry Sawyer endeavour[illegible] to take over and at halfway was lying 4th but he too gave way in the end to finish 6th with a fast-finishing Linstead close behind. Clive Shippen and Eric Gebbett had a tremendous tussle with Alexander of Highgate in the latter stages and with half a mile to go appeared to have won the day, for Clive had put in a fast finish to break we[illegible] away and Eric was chasing hard. On reaching the finishing straight however, the Highgate man put in a last desperate effort and was successful in splitting our two runners. Fortunately this alone did not quite decide the result. Charlie Walker and John Davies backed up well, with 6 to score we would have won. Pos Name Club Time 1. G. Brown Highgate 31:02 2. K. Harland Cambridge H. 31:15 3. F. Mellor Ponders End 31:26 6. B. items.s: THE CLUB SEVEN Report and result of the club 7 miles cross-country championship, won by Barry Sawyer, who also took second in the handicap. A field of about 25 faced the starter and was soon away to a brisk start. On the way out to the village John Davies led the field whilst in the bunch behind a few private battles were taking place. (I understand that at this stage a man named Penney was causing some comment by being in a forward position in the field) At the end of the first lap Barry Sawyer had opened up a useful lead with C. Shippen and R. Linstead "enjoying" a real ding-dong battle. Then came Walker, Davies, Moore, Miller, Penney, Thresher, and D. Jones with the rest of the field well strung out behind them. At the finish Sawyer ran in a well-deserved winner and at the same time took second place in the handicap. R. Linstead just managed to pip C. Shippen for second place, C. Walker ran steadily in fourth position, John Davies showed a glimpse of his old form, and John Moore showed that he was beginning to find his feet again. Perhaps this win is sufficient justification of Barry's spartan training schedule and we hope that his success augurs well for Belgrave too. A.W.P. Pos Name Time 1. B. Sawyer 40:40 2. R. items.s: WALKING NEWS Introduction to the walking news praising Ray Middleton and George Williams for filling the gaps left by Stan Vickers and Eric Hall. In the absence, temporary we hope, of Stan Vickers and Eric Hall it might have been thought that the Bels would have been content to rest on their laurels. But not a bit of it. Ray Middleton and George Williams have filled these two gaps admirably, gained international colours, and formed the mainstay of several championship teams. If 1962, European Games year, finds these two maintaining their form and also sees Stan and Eric back with us on the track and on the road, then this surely would prove our year of years and our team would certainly be invincible. items.s: AUGUST 12th 1961 INTERNATIONAL LUGARNO TROPHY (Central Zone) Report and result of the Lugano Trophy (European Cup walking) zonal round in August 1961, where George Williams was fifth in the 20 km and Ray Middleton third in the 50 km on his Great Britain debut. Belgrave provided two of Britain's six men in this 20 kilos and 50 kilos competition in this triangular international with Belgium and Germany, (East/West combined), the first round of the Europa Cup. George Williams walked the 20 kilos to gain his second international vest and Ray Middleton made his debut for Great Britain in the 50. In the morning Ken Matthews led from start to finish to win the 20 by over 3 minutes in most convincing fashion. George fought hard all the way but had finally to concede three places to a German trio and so finished in 5th position. At lunch therefore, East and West Germany led Great Britain by the narrow margin of 2 points. The 50 kilos was also walked at a fast pace and provided another quite comfortable British victory, this time for Don Thompson. Ray Middleton walked most doggedly, moved up into second spot, and was then passed at 40 kilos by Sakowski (Germany). Ray held on in fine fashion and resisted the final challenge of yet another German Astroth. The 50 kilos result ensured a British victory and a place in the final at Lugano on October 14th. SEPTEMBER 9th We were out in force in an attempt to regain this team title that we lost some three years ago. In fact the final issue was decided by the position of the fourth scoring men of Belgrave and Surrey. John Keown beat his respective opposite number and so won the day for the Bels. In the early stages George Beecham, Ken Bailey and Ray Hall walked together, but the pack broke up at ten miles with Ken chasing after the leaders. Fred Denny and John Morris both retired in the first half of the race. Harry Shields " just out for a stroll" finally managed to beat second class standard by 5 secs. after 53 miles. The Belgrave champs. was eventually won by Ray Hall who caught Ken Bailey at Albourne Green and from there onwards there was never more than two or three yards between the two of them. Ray's greater experience however, won him the day by one second after 53 miles(you must sprint when you can see the sea). Ken Bailey walked magnificently in his first Brighton, George Beecham took third place after a steady race, and John Keown backed up well. Thanks must go to those who assisted our walkers, to mention just a few, Eric & Mavis Hall, Jack Goswell, Eric Beecham, and Don Bartliff. Pos Name (Club) Time 1. D. Thompson (MET W.C.) 7:39.57 2. items.h: OCTOBER 14th - MIDDLETON AND WILLIAMS HELP BRITAIN TO WIN WORLD CUP
items.sum: Report and result of the final of the walking World Cup (Lugano Trophy) on 14 October 1961, won by Great Britain on a tie-break, with Middleton fourth in the 50 km and Williams third in the 20 km.
items.s: OCTOBER 14th - MIDDLETON AND WILLIAMS HELP BRITAIN TO WIN WORLD CUP Report and result of the final of the walking World Cup (Lugano Trophy) on 14 October 1961, won by Great Britain on a tie-break, with Middleton fourth in the 50 km and Williams third in the 20 km. In the finals of this World Cup Competition at Lugano we emerged as the first winners of this trophy. Italy, after a great start in which Pamich beat Olympic winner Don Thompson by as much as five minutes in the 50 kilometre failed to stay the course and put up a comparatively poor showing in the shorter events. It therefore became a straight fight between Sweden and ourselves with Hungary last of the four. In the 20 kilometres, Ken Matthews set off at his usual fast pace, and rapidly built up a big lead over the second man Back of Sweden. Although Ken lost some ground nearing home he still won by some 400 metres and George Williams exceeded all hopes by beating some really hot opposition for third. With a tie on the aggregate of the two events the rule was invoked giving preference to the country which first finished the man in the 50 kilometres event and that was Great Britain.
