items.label: May 1962
items.sum: Humorous sketch about a veteran timekeeper, Archibald Fortescue Tidworthy, lecturing novice timekeepers and then failing to time a record mile because his watch was not wound.
items.s: GOOD TIMING? Humorous sketch about a veteran timekeeper, Archibald Fortescue Tidworthy, lecturing novice timekeepers and then failing to time a record mile because his watch was not wound. "Timekeeping's not quite so simple as it looks" said that well-known Belgravian, Archibald Fortescue Tidworthy, as we went out onto the field, "but I expect you'll soon get used to it." "I feel quite nervous." said Sparrow. "It's the first time that I've done any serious timekeeping, you know Tidders." "Oh I shouldn't worry too much if I were you." said Tidworthy. "Practice makes perfect, you know, and you'll get plenty of that here. I'm a far better timekeeper now than when I started ten years ago". "I suppose," said Sparrow, "that at first you tend to gaze at the watch rather than watching the runners." "Oh its quite a thrill," said Tidworthy,"when you clock a record. I can remember breaking five records in one afternoon. In fact, we might well break the mile again today." "Oh I don't think that's very likely." said Sparrow. The first race was the 100 yds. Tidworthy returned 10.4. Sparrow and I both returned 10.3. Tidworthy shook his head indulgently. "Well, we're obliged to take your time as there's two of you in agreement. But you both seem to be committing the usual beginners' mistake. You've started too late. Remember now - go by the pistol flash and not the report. Light travels faster than sound." "I suppose," countered Sparrow, "that's why we know what you are going to say before you say it." In the furlong Tidworthy returned 23.2. Sparrow and I made it 23.0. "There you are," snapped Tidworthy, "you're both too fast again." "Couldn't you possibly be just a little...well...slow?" enquired Sparrow gently. "Everybody makes mistakes," said Tidworthy philosophically, "but I doubt whether I would have made the same mistake twice. No, you're both catching them too late. Try opening your mouths a little - it's an established medical fact that this minimizes the shock to the nervous system, brought about by the loud report and ensures a wholly more responsive reaction." "Well, it would be difficult for anyone to catch you with your mouth shut" quipped Sparrow. The following race, the 440 yds. revealed a complete reversal of form. I had 50.1, Sparrow had 50.0 whereas Tidworthy had 49.9 sec. Tidworthy scrutinized the watches in a careful silence. Quite onviously it was he who was now playing for time. "Your mouth," said Sparrow quickly, "it wasn't open wide enough. Try harder next time, with a bit of luck you may dislocate it." "Errors do sometimes creep in at the finish as well as the start" replied Tidworthy, quite oblivious of his critics. "Beginners become rather over-anxious you know, and press the button before the runner breasts the tape. Quite an understandable mistake, you know." "If we had done that," said Sparrow,"wouldn't our times have been faster than yours, and not slower?" "Yes, so they would." Tidworthy admitted after a moments consideration. "What I actually meant to say was that the beginner becomes enthralled by the struggle being enacted before his very eyes, and actually presses the button only after the worsted has been broken." "You're better than Houdini for getting out of awkward corners!" replied the now exasperated Sparrow. "Well," said Tidworthy, "I hope we can agree better in the mile. Braithwaite has a splendid chance of breaking the existing record." "Personally, I think Tidders' chances are much higher" Sparrow said quietly to me. The mile was duly won by Braithwaite who finished impressively to win by some 15 yards. The timekeepers looked intently at their watches. "4:15.6" I said. "4:15.7" said Sparrow almost by way of confirmation, "That's a second inside the Club record. Nice running by Braithwaite". We turned to the remaining member of our timing trio. No response. He was standing gazing wide-mouthed at his watch, which lay in his hand like a tea plate. "Heavens above," said Sparrow, "he really has dislocated his jaw this time." "You chaps must be mad," said Tidworthy at last. "He's broken the record easily - 3:59.9. Its fantastic. Its world class. What a classic piece of timing, and you muffed it, you duffers!" Sparrow gently took the 'tea-plate' from the shaking hands of the excited Archibald Fortescue Tidworthy. He pressed the button twice. Nothing. "It's stopped." he said. "You forgot to wind it up."

items.sum: Report of the 1962 National cross-country championship at Blackpool on 10 March, won by Gerry North, with the Belgrave seniors 17th, plus the party's evening and long journey home.
items.s: THE 1962 NATIONAL Report of the 1962 National cross-country championship at Blackpool on 10 March, won by Gerry North, with the Belgrave seniors 17th, plus the party's evening and long journey home. March 10th - The spirit of 'National' day has still to return to Belgrave at least, as far as the older runners are concerned. Although the Seniors "improved" on last year's showing by 4 places and 168 points they still amassed a total of 1218 in finishing 17th! But for the ever-readiness of Joe Dooley and Don MacLean to fill gaps whenever called upon we would have been unable to finish a team. Injuries to Kerr, Dabbs and Davies and the absence of our usual spear-head,Pat Newell, did not augur well for our chances before we had even left London. This year's course was held over the Royal Lancashire Agricultural Show ground at Blackpool, and the going was fast and flat. Walker and Shippen both got good starts and after a mile were in the first 100, but they failed to make ground in their usual manner and instead , steadily lost places. Ron Linstead and Barry Sawyer started steadily and moved through the field well, Ron in particular was well into his stride. Eric Gebbett who has been steadily approaching his old form was our 5th man home in 219th place, but we had to go back to a courageous Joe Dooley (426) for our 6th scorer, it was this alone that enabled our old rivals Birchfield to beat us by 2 places; their 6th man being none other than our old friend Len Orton who was well below form in 278th place. It gave all Belgravians great hope for next year to see the dazzling run of Gerry North. With an injury-free Bill Kerr to compete also, we can expect a considerable improvement. On this occasion, it is not mere wishful thinking to say they would certainly have enabled us to split Woodford and T.V.H. who finished 6th and 7th. Most of the Belgravian party spent the evening at the "Wintergarden" ballroom where the International teams were introduced to the dancers. Following the traditional meal of 'pie and chips' the special excursion left for London at 12.30a.m. Activities on the homeward journey ranged from solo whist to cricket and all-in wrestling! The journey was considerably prolonged due to numerous delays en route and the tired travellors arrived at Euston just 24 hours after their departure the previous morning. Apart from our Youths this was not a memorable day for our runners, but one of our team will remember it well - Eric Gebbett; not for a 9 mile race but for a seven mile walk! Eric, who lives at Leighton Buzzard, had to alight at Bletchley on the homeward journey; the only scheduled stop of the trip. So a tired Eric set off on foot for home at 5.a.m. with a heavy running bag due South for 7 miles. How would he have felt just minutes later had he known that our train was held up in Leighton Buzzard station for no less than 40 minutes? items.sum: Bill Lucas's report of the Ilford road relay, where an injury-hit Belgrave 'A' team finished eighth behind record-setting Portsmouth, with stage times for both Belgrave teams.
items.s: THE ILFORD ROAD RELAY Bill Lucas's report of the Ilford road relay, where an injury-hit Belgrave 'A' team finished eighth behind record-setting Portsmouth, with stage times for both Belgrave teams. BILL LUCAS REPORTS:- We have a very good record in this race and during the past few years have contested the leading places with considerable vigour and success. 1962 however, was not to be our year for Bill Kerr, Alan Black,Ken Miller and Charlie Dabbs were all on the injured list and we had to call upon reserves who, although putting everything they had into their running, were not quite fit enough, and had to concede places. The finishing position of eighth was most disappointing. Eric Gebbett gave us a fairly good start in his inimitable style and brought us into 10th place. Charlie Walker went off second but was far from his best - something on his mind I believe and a leg injury as well, which definitely affected his running - and we were back to twelfth when Ron Linstead set off. Ron turned in our fastest time of the day and brought us well to the fore by gaining six places. At this stage Reading were in the lead with Polytechnic second, and Ponders End third, our deficit being only 50 secs. Clive Shippen took the fourth leg and gained one more place to move us up to fifth. At this point Portsmouth, the eventual winners, had come into the picture only 15 secs. behind Poly, who had now taken the lead. John Thresher held his position on Stage 5 but we were now 1 min.43secs. behind the new leaders T.V.H. who had taken the lead, thanks to a fine run by Haith. John Davies on leg 6 also held on to fifth place but was a little disappointing. John's capabilities never really come to light in this sort of event and with his basic turn of speed he should be able to do 18 mins, for this lap, but lack of confidence in his own powers seems to be his biggest enemy. The seventh and eighth legs were taken by reserves, and although both John Moore and David Jones flogged themselves to the utmost, they were not really fit enough for this type of competition, and we had to drop back to ninth some 6 mins. behind Portsmouth when Barry Sawyer took over. Barry had been suffering from leg trouble and was still not back to his best. He ran steadily, but could gain no ground on the leaders, nor any places. Don Maclean was in one of his "on form" moods for the last leg and ran well to gain one place - given another quarter of a mile he would have undoubtedly caught the Walton man ahead. We also fielded a 'B' team but unfortunately could only complete 8 legs. A new member, Laurie O'Hara, excelled himself by running the leg in 18.58. This was particularly good as he was 40 secs. behind the team in front when he took over - not only did he catch this team but also made up another place. Laurie is obviously a fine discovery and could be a great asset to us. Chris Steer also ran very well to record 19.04 in his first Senior relay. W.E.L. Day's Fastest 1.Haith (T.V.H) 17:27 2. items.sum: Report of the Club 5¾ mile race for the Wimbledon Cup, won by Charlie Walker, with an unofficial fastest time by second-claim member Gerry North and the handicap won by Chas. Henn.
items.s: THE WIMBLEDON CUP Report of the Club 5¾ mile race for the Wimbledon Cup, won by Charlie Walker, with an unofficial fastest time by second-claim member Gerry North and the handicap won by Chas. Henn. WALKER WINS CLUB '5¾' The biggest eye-opener of the day was Gerry North's remarkable time of 27:15. This performance, although unofficial, as Gerry is still second claim - was no less than 41 secs. inside Ranjit Bhatia's course record! How many of our older runners ever dreamt they'd see the approach of 27 mins for this course? But perhaps they've been dreaming of Belgrave-bred athletes in which case they have yet to be surprised, for Charlie Walker's 29:27 was the fastest the rest could produce. The smallest field for some time set off at the usual fast pace with Gerry North endeavouring to get clear right at the start. Fireworks were expected when Bill Kerr clung to North like a leech for the first one mile lap; and when Kerr actually overtook the National cross-country champion a ding-dong battle was fully expected. However, approaching the two mile mark, the Scotsman retired from the race through feeling the effects of his recent achilles injury; a sad disappointment. But they will meet again-many times we hope. The most interesting features of the race further back were the forward running of John Thresher, Laurie O'Hara (a novice, competitively) and Chris Steer. A few eyebrows were also raised at the smooth even-paced run "out of the bag" by Arthur Bruce. With a mile to go Thresher led the Championship field from O'Hara and Walker, but Charlie produced the strongest finish, and thus had his name inscribed on the "Wimbledon" cup for the first time but, it should be added, against one of his slowest times. As a result of this race the pundits forecast we would be fielding our weakest 'Brighton' team since the war. Only time( and a few more pages) will tell. A popular winner of the handicap was our "Whitehall man" Chas. Henn, who owed his success on this occasion to leaving his umbrella with the Starter! * went off course. Pos Name Time 1. C. items.sum: Musically themed report of the Cambridge Harriers 6 x 3½ mile relay at Bexley on 24 March, where only ten Belgravians turned up and the 'A' team finished eighth (results on page 22).
items.s: 'Music hath charms'............or .......10 BELS AT BEXLEY Musically themed report of the Cambridge Harriers 6 x 3½ mile relay at Bexley on 24 March, where only ten Belgravians turned up and the 'A' team finished eighth (results on page 22). CAMBRIDGE H. 6 x 3½ miles relay. Belgrave were at least notable for one thing on March 24th, lack of Belgravians. Unless we had four ghost teams taking part, it appeared that only ten of our 42 entries were in attendance! Yes, believe it or not,just ten. Thus only two of our six teams started, comprising an 'A' sextet and a 'D' quartet.(Musical instruments would have rounded off the day nicely) We put the piccolo on the first stage - "Chirpy" Charlie Walker - who put in several extra notes on this occasion to record a sequel to Tchaikovsky's overture with 18:13, in a close 8th place. Ron Linstead struck a similar rhythm which took him three places forward to a fine 18:22; 17 secs. behind the leaders, Portsmouth. Young, Chris Steer,in the 'A' team for the first time, was unable to keep the tempo going but, nevertheless, broke 19 mins. in his first race over the course - it will not be many seasons before he cracks the magical 18 min. barrier at both Bexley and Ilford. The 4th movement of this Belgrave composition was played by Barry Sawyer who at last seemed to be rid of the numerous injuries which had recently been chasing themselves up and down each of his legs. On this occasion, however, Barry's legs did the chasing and Haith of T.V.H. was the main sufferer. His time of 18:30 gave John Thresher a send-off in 7th position. John was destined to play his part in something of a minor key but nevertheless, his time of 18:37 enabled us to move up into sixth position just in front of T.V.H. Unfortunately the course was a little on the hilly side for Don Maclean who waltzed rather than quick-stepped, and we had finally to be content with eighth place some fourteen seconds behind Mitcham's 7th. This team will undoubtedly be called upon for many encores, as it was made up of six of our most reliable Club-men. We can thank them that Belgrave's name was not completely besmirched. items.h: BELS. 13th IN NATIONAL RELAY WORST PERFORMANCE SINCE 1927
items.sum: Olympian's stage-by-stage report of the London to Brighton (National) road relay, where Belgrave finished 13th, their worst for over 30 years, relieved by Bill Kerr's club record on the Hand Cross stage; with a photo and a cartoon.
items.s: BELS. 13th IN NATIONAL RELAY WORST PERFORMANCE SINCE 1927 Olympian's stage-by-stage report of the London to Brighton (National) road relay, where Belgrave finished 13th, their worst for over 30 years, relieved by Bill Kerr's club record on the Hand Cross stage; with a photo and a cartoon. Olympian reports: A dismal tale - in fact the most dismal that has been recorded for any Brighton Relay for over 30 years. Briefly - thirteenth on the first leg and thirteenth, 10 mins. 57 secs. behind, at the end. What happened in between hardly bears relating,for not even a strong following wind could produce good times on any leg except the long stretch beyond Hand Cross which was again taken by Bill Kerr. It was quite a tonic to see him loping along uphill and down dale to record 28:35 which was a new Club record and a time beaten only by Internationals of such class as Kilby(Coventry) Bullivant (Derby) Craig (Blackpool) Freary (Bolton) and Tulloh (Portsmouth). Other bouquets go to Alan Black for a good effort after only 6 weeks' training, Clive Shippen for his fastest time yet up Dale Hill, Laurie O'Hara new to this type of sport ( football is his game) for a very steady performance on the tenth and Charlie Walker in his 24th consecutive Brighton for a brave run in difficult circumstances against heavy opposition. STAGE I - John Davies (21:16, 13th fastest) The first leg was led home by Hammond of Coventry (2nd in this year's National Youths Cross-country) with John lagging 55 seconds behind having lost touch before Chelsea Bridge. I think John will agree that he was well on the way to being beaten before he left the dressing room - confidence in one's ability to win races is a must if success is to be achieved. STAGE II - John Thresher (25:21, 14th fastest)John could make no impression on the teams ahead and we slipped slowly further behind so that by the time Mitcham was reached Charlie Walker was confronted with a leeway of 2mins. and 13 secs. STAGE III - Charlie Walker (29:04, 12th fastest) Although losing more ground on the leaders and despite looking a trifle jaded along the Purley Way Charlie made up four places with a well-judged run on what is one of the hardest legs. Already by this time we were revealing our shortage of "big guns". STAGE IV - Eric Gebbett (25:52, 16th fastest)Eric who had been switched to the fourth stage only a day before the race seemed to lack fire in the early part of his run but came through to finish well. He was forced to give away a place to Mick Firth of S.L.H. who ran second fastest on this particular stage. At the end of this leg we were nearly five minutes adrift - the leaders at this point being Bristol with Derby second and Portsmouth 3rd. These 3 clubs fought out the lead for the rest of the race. STAGE V - Barry Sawyer (22:28 17th fastest) Barry who for weeks has been troubled with strained muscles was not at his best and before the end of the Redhill stage was again limping badly. STAGE VI - David Cocks (14:04 13th fastest) "what a position to be in — no-one in sight" is probably the thought that occured to David who had been allocated the short stage to Horley. He usually finds himself nearer the leaders when running with "Tom's boys" but although not excelling himself he was certainly hot disgraced and did sufficient to show that there would be many more places in Belgrave Brighton teams. STAGE VII - Alan Black (18:27,7 th. fastest) Alan, making a welcome return after suffering a cracked ankle bone, was also well out of touch with the team ahead but he soon set about closing the 74 sec. gap between himself and Blackpool and close it he did to gain one place as Gatwick Airport was reached. The 6½ minutes between us and Bristol, still in the lead, had reached formidable proportions. STAGE VIII - Ron Linstead (30:51 15th fastest) Ron could hardly have picked a tougher task than dealing first with Gerry North, who put up the fastest time of the day on this leg,and then Hogan of Polytechnic who both swept past in quick succession. This was certainly not Ron's day but he took us to within striking distance of Birchfield, our old rivals, who had up to this point been well ahead of us. STAGE IX - Bill Kerr (28:35 6th fastest) Bill was not in the least dismayed by our plight and set off after the Birchfield runner in great style. He must have been astonished when Shelley of N.Staffs appeared on his shoulder having made up 16 secs. in the run down Handcross Hill. Shelley soon paid for his exuberance and fell away to the extent of a full minute. Bill, running as well as we know he can, passed the Birchfield man and gradually closed the gap on Richards of Poly. His pace at the end was quite incredible to watch - an excellent performance. STAGE X - Laurie O'Hara (20:27 14th fastest) Laurie who has only been a member for a few months gave up a chance to play in an important football match to run for us and it was soon obvious that we have in Laurie a real discovery. Steadily he closed the gap on Ralph Dunkley of Poly and failed by only four seconds to make up the 49 sec. deficit with which he started. With the right training and more racing experience.Laurie could well become one of our leading runners within the next 12 months. STAGE XI - Clive Shippen (20:23, 7th fastest) Clive who must know Dale Hill like the back of his hand soon caught and passed the Poly runner and then proceeded to pull right away but the gap ahead was far too great to get within striking distance of the 12th team Mitcham. STAGE XII - Don Maclean (17:50, 9th fastest) Don looking like a champion devoured the stretch across Preston Park and although naturally tiring at the end held on well to put up one of his best road performances for the Club and to give a pleasant surprise to all the doubting Thomases. This race has proved that no longer can Belgrave hope to do well with a team devoid of stars. We have always prided ourselves on our strength in depth, but we have come to the end of this particular road and must now build up our reputation on something more than the good average club man. With just two top-class performers we would have taken at least fifth place in this race. Derby and Portsmouth at present seem to be in a class of their own and virtually unassailable, but the circle must turn and it may well be that Belgrave could take their place as of old. This can only be accomplished if everyone trains as they have never trained before with the sole object of putting Belgrave back on the map both on road and country - it can be done!!! items.s: Boxed news of overseas members: Ranjit Bhatia regaining form in India and Mal Robinson running for the University of Southern Louisiana. Ranjit Bhatia writes again to say that he is gradually regaining his old form. He won his State 5,000 metres final in 15:19:2 and then in the Indian Championships finished 3rd in the 1500 metres final with 4:00:7. Says Ranjit, "These are pretty mediocre times, but I feel glad that I am on the up again" - and so are we. * * * * * Mal Robinson, we hear, has been doing plenty of studying, travelling and running in his first year at the University of Southern Louisianna,U.S.A It is rumoured he has not found time to smoke or drink for six solid weeks! Malcolm got off to a very good start this season by finishing second in his College Championships with 4:10·7, his best ever. Keep at it Mal. we only take back sub-4 min. men from State-side! items.h: A word from your TRACK SECRETARY
items.sum: Track Secretary Dave Shepherd previews the 1962 track season, the club championships at Hurlingham and a planned 1963 tour to Copenhagen, illustrated with a starting-practice cartoon.
items.s: A word from your TRACK SECRETARY Track Secretary Dave Shepherd previews the 1962 track season, the club championships at Hurlingham and a planned 1963 tour to Copenhagen, illustrated with a starting-practice cartoon. The track season is once again with us. We have a very full fixture list and I am sure all members interested in the Track will find enough competition. We do hope that all members will co-operate with us this season, especially when notified of being selected to run in team races. Please do not forget to give good notice if you are not able to fulfill an engagement, so that the reserve can be given a chance to run. Our Championships this year will be on Saturday 26th May 1962 at Hurlingham Track. We should like to see more Senior Sprinters this year, also more support from the Field Events. Our two-mile track team, with Gerry North included should do well this year, but our other two-mile runners will have to train hard to give Gerry the support he is worthy of. The Fixture Cards will soon be circulated, but if you have any doubts about fixtures, get in touch with the Track Captain, Bob Taylor, or myself, and we will do our best to answer your queries. I am pleased to inform members that we are making arrangements for a Tour in 1963 to Copenhagen, during which we intend to have two matches with Foreign Clubs. For this tour we will join forces with a Ladies Club. Date for tour - last week in August, first week in September 1963, approximate cost, £40.0.0d. If you are interested, please let me know, and I will let you have more details. Wishing you all a successfull season - DAVE SHEPHERD. DONT YOU THINK YOU MIGHT TRY A SLIGHTLY MORE ORTHODOX START SLUDGE? Starting practice is with us once more! Starting practice is with us once more! items.label: November 1962
items.sum: Editorial marking the end of the club's 75th year, praising its healthy spirit and younger members, introducing the frontispiece photos loaned by Syd King, and explaining the late issue and new editorial address.
items.s: EDITORIAL Editorial marking the end of the club's 75th year, praising its healthy spirit and younger members, introducing the frontispiece photos loaned by Syd King, and explaining the late issue and new editorial address. The Club's 75th year approaches its end. We now enter the final quarter of our first century with the hope and prospect of reaching heights even greater than the many we have attained during the last 7½ decades. As an Amateur Club we have a decidedly healthy look and an excellent club spirit. This has become increasingly noticeable over the last year or so and is in no small way due to our younger members, many of whom are taking an active part in the administration of Belgrave. Young faces are appearing on Committee, progressive ideas are being put forward and there has been a marked improvement in our Socials and catering arrangments. Our athletes can feel confident that they have the backing of an Organisation which will enable them to gain maximum results from their training. Unfortunately, we do not possess any photographs of the Club's very early days but we do reproduce as our frontispiece two pictures kindly loaned to us by Syd King which we think will be of interest. Should any of our older members have any early photographs suitable for publication we shall be delighted to hear from them. Since our last edition the Mitchell half of the editorship has married the charming lady who typewrites all our material, whilst the Shippen half has moved house. There is, of course, no sinister connection between the two occurrences (!) but we mention them to explain the late appearance of this issue and also to draw your attention to the new editorial address. We hope that 1963 will see the regular quarterly appearance of 'The Belgravian'. To accomplish this we shall need the co-operation of our contributors and we appeal for all matter to be sent to us immediately it becomes available. Correspondence is welcome from all sources, particularly our distant members. Syd King Syd King Mitchell Mitchell Shippen Shippen Belgrave Harriers 75th Anniversary 1962

items.label: November 1962
items.sum: The Hon. Secretary's notes recording the deaths of founder member J.H. Martyn and Dick Best, thanking retiring treasurer Sid Roberts, and congratulating Ray Middleton, Ray Hall, Derek Boosey, Ron Linstead and Gerry North on selections.
items.s: HON. SEC'S NOTES The Hon. Secretary's notes recording the deaths of founder member J.H. Martyn and Dick Best, thanking retiring treasurer Sid Roberts, and congratulating Ray Middleton, Ray Hall, Derek Boosey, Ron Linstead and Gerry North on selections. Our Annual report advised the death of our last surviving founder-member (as far as is known) Mr. J.H. Martyn, at the age of 95 years. He has told how the Club was formed after a visit to an Athletics meeting at Kennington Oval, and how he was elected the first Club Captain. The changes that have taken place in the intervening seventy five years are tremendous, both in general terms and in the field of athletics. It seems incredible that the Club cross-country headquarters were once at Battersea Rise; and that our sprinters showed their speed along the Embankment, relatively traffic-free. ☆ ☆ ☆ We also mourn the passing of R.W. (Dick) Best, a Life Member and Vice President of the Club, and donor of our 880 yards Championship Cup. Dick came from the Westminster area which saw the origins of our Club; and between the Wars he was a very popular figure, with a great sense of humour and inherent charm, at hundreds of Meetings in the Home Counties. Dick had a standing order to be entered in all Club meeting running events and cheerfully paid up all his dues at the end of the season. He was a great supporter of the Club in many ways and we shall miss his cheery smile. (Cont'd.) ☆ ☆ ☆ It is proper that we should express our sincere thanks to the Club Officers who were not re-elected or did not seek re-election at the Annual General Meeting, for all their work on our behalf. Particularly, our very genuine appreciation of Sid Roberts' magnificent work must be placed on record For twenty-two years Sid has served us in our Club in one office or another; and since 1952 he has been our highly-efficient Hon. Treasurer. Business reasons compel Sid's retirement from office; and we are indeed grateful for the great service he has rendered in so many different ways over such a long period. ☆ ☆ ☆ Our heartiest congratulations go to Ray Middleton and Ray Hall who were selected to represent Great Britain on the European Championships at Belgrade in the 50 Kilometres Walk. Also to Derek Boosey who well earned his selection for the Triple Jump in the Great Britain v. Finland match. ☆ ☆ ☆ Ron Linstead also merits our congratulations on being selected as one of the four British Long distance runners to represent the Road Runners Club in the Comrades Marathon in South Africa. Despite being out of luck on the day, Ron still managed to be fifth man home in this classic long distance event. ☆ ☆ ☆ Gerry North has been doing great deeds in our name recently and we have every hope that he will lead our cross country and road-relay teams to many many successes. We could not hope to have a finer runner for our Cross country Captain; and if Gerry is given the support that it is in our power to give, Belgrave can be very prominent indeed in all the major events. How about having three men in the International Cross-country team next March? A.A.H. A.A.H. A.A.H. J.H. Martyn Mr. J.H. Martyn R.W. (Dick) Best R.W. (Dick) Best R.W. items.label: November 1962
items.sum: Profile of the new club President Dave Shepherd, recalling his running in the 1930s and his long service as Social and Track Hon. Secretary and now Hon. Treasurer.
items.s: THE PRESIDENT — D.M.SHEPHERD Profile of the new club President Dave Shepherd, recalling his running in the 1930s and his long service as Social and Track Hon. Secretary and now Hon. Treasurer. We congratulate ourselves most heartily on having for our President this year one who has developed in the true Belgravian tradition, - one who has not spared himself in service to the Club over many years. This trait of long and devoted service has ever been present in our Presidents, and Dave has certainly helped in a hundred different ways in his thirty years of membership. Joining us in the early 1930s Dave was to be found at most of our fixtures and in 1934, he was second man home for the Club in our fourth team in the Southern Junior Cross country championship. Studies now claimed his full attention for many years, and although often seen, he was unable to devote the time to training that membership of our teams demanded. He persevered with his studies, showing that determination we have seen in Club affairs, and after years of hard work became an expert in the field of heating and ventilating engineering. Now began his great work for the Club and he has served us in a variety of ways. His technical knowledge has been of the greatest value to us, he was an excellent Social Hon. Secretary for many years, a member of the Belgrave Hall Sub Committee, and in recent years has carried through admirably the task of Track Hon. Secretary. Life Membership was conferred upon him some years ago and now we honour him as our new President. For good measure, and this is typical of him, he has also become an Hon. Treasurer in succession to Sid Roberts! Dave would be the first to acknowledge the great help he has received from his wife (the present President of the Surrey County W.A.A.A.) his late Father-in-Law Dick Savage, and Mrs. Savage. Belgrave was ever in the heart of the Savage family; and Dave quickly learned to share their regard for Belgrave and to make his contribution to our Club. I would particularly acknowledge the great part he played with re-planning the Belgrave Hall when the freehold was acquired; and his attention to detail and the great assistance he afforded when we were planning ahead and battling with the Ministry for building licences. He has certainly deserved well of Belgrave, and his personal qualities and devotion to the Club will ensure that we have a very worthy President indeed. We shall be proud to serve under his leadership. A.A.H. Dave Shepherd D.M.SHEPHERD D.M.SHEPHERD Dave A.A.H. A.A.H. items.label: November 1962
items.sum: New President Dave Shepherd's message for the club's 75th year, urging members to support fixtures and socials, with a postscript as Treasurer asking for subscriptions, and his photograph.
items.s: The President's Message New President Dave Shepherd's message for the club's 75th year, urging members to support fixtures and socials, with a postscript as Treasurer asking for subscriptions, and his photograph. I am most honoured to be elected as your President for this, the 75th year of the Club, and I am looking forward to a most enjoyable year in office. Our Hon. Secretary has referred to this year as the time for a possible 'break through' and I would very much like to see this achieved. Success is not easy, all must work for it, Athlete, Coach, Official and Spectator, with team spirit and one aim - to be first past the post. I am confident we shall see improved results. I should like to see all members making full use of the facilities the Club has to offer, it is of course, up to you, and if you are in any doubt you only have to ask any member of the Club committee, I know they will put themselves out to help. Do not forget that Belgrave is the best Club in Amateur Athletics, that is why I joined, and I know that this was your reason also. Keep the standard up. the part you play in club life is just as important as any other member's. Will you also do your best to support the fixtures arranged by your Section Secretary, especially if you are asked to represent the Club. A lot of work goes into the organising of the meetings and you let yourself and most important, the Club down if you fail to turn out without due notice. Social functions also need your support. If you have not yet had an evening with your fellow members, make an effort this year, I am sure you will enjoy yourself, and don't forget to bring the wife or girl friend. Lastly, I do wish you all a most successful and enjoyable season. Dave Shepherd. P.S. I have asked the Editors to allow me space in this Issue to introduce myself to you all as your new Treasurer. This is a new job for me and I know that you will do your best to help me. May I suggest the best possible way to do just this? SEND YOUR SUBS, to me NOW. DON'T WAIT FOR ME TO WRITE TO YOU. Dave Shepherd, 104 Florence Road, Wimbledon S.W.19. Seniors £1.10.0d. Juniors 12/6d. Youths 5/-d. Dave Shepherd Dave Shepherd Belgrave Harriers 75th Anniversary 1962 Florence Road, Wimbledon S.W.19

items.label: November 1962
items.sum: Report of the club's 75th anniversary dinner and dance at the Ardington Rooms, Clapham Junction, with the speeches and toasts including the handover from Arthur Penny to new President Dave Shepherd.
items.s: '75th Year' Dinner Report of the club's 75th anniversary dinner and dance at the Ardington Rooms, Clapham Junction, with the speeches and toasts including the handover from Arthur Penny to new President Dave Shepherd. There was something extra special about this year's Dinner for although it was held in the same place as last year, the Ardington Rooms, Clapham Junction, and although there was the usual array of familiar faces it did mark the 75th anniversary of the Club. Despite it being a bleak rainy evening this does not mean that the spirit of the occasion was at all dampened. This is one Club event when competition is put aside and everybody makes the best of having a good time. After the Dinner itself we settled back over coffee, wine or in some cases cigars, (Havana?) to listen to the speeches. I think most people will agree that after-dinner Speakers vary in standard considerably and that after a good meal sleep is never far away in any case. But we were fortunate in our choice. A.J.C. Kendall, B.E.M., of the Southern Counties Athletic Association, proposed the toast to the Club and in doing so, drew attention to the enormous amount that Belgrave has contributed to the sport of athletics. We were also praised for our continual efforts in recent years in promoting numerous junior and youth events. It was appropriate that the response on behalf of the Club should be made by our Hon. Sec. unofficial historian, and nigh-on Mr. Belgrave, Alf Harley. Alf mentioned several respected and notable Belgravians present including 82 year old Harry Evans (still without his raincoat), K. O'Kell, A. Foster, and E. Macher and then told us a simple story that in some ways exemplified the true Belgrave spirit. Ted Goode, a member in the 1890s heard of Belgrave, wanted to join, and in order to save the 1/-d. membership fee walked to work from Chelsea to Baker St. each day until he had the necessary sum. It was through keeness and determination such as this that Belgrave has grown into the powerful and successful Club it now is. Sid Roberts proposed the toast to our Guests and singled out for special tribute the mums, wives and girl-friends present. D. Goodman of Surrey A.A. replied on the Guests' behalf and in his speech described Belgrave as a big-hearted Club and then went on to recall several happy moments he has spent with us and also several of those so-called "Social Runs" that he has enjoyed(?) in our Company. L.W.Woodcock of the Road Walking Association also replied for the guests and in the shortest speech of the evening heartily endorsed Mr. Goodman's opinions of Belgrave Harriers. Our retiring President Arthur 'Nutty' Penny then proposed a toast to his successor, Dave Martin Shepherd and Mrs. Shepherd. Dave replied and in his own cheeky fashion told us an amusing anecdote of a Club outing to Littlehampton by charabanc some years' ago when it rained 'cats and dogs' all day with the result that they all returned home wet both inside and out! A bouquet was then presented by Mrs. Shepherd to Mrs. Penny, a simple but admirable gesture from one President's wife to another. Dinner downed and speeches over, tables were cleared away in preparation for dancing. Waltz or rock, tango or twist, everyone had a go and as is usual when things are going with a swing, it was soon 12.00 midnight and unfortunately time to go home. It may be our 75th year but if this Dinner and Dance is anything to go by, there's plenty of life left in the 'Old Dog' yet, and I am sure that all who attended would agree that this was a most enjoyable Club evening and that next year's 'Do' will be another sell-out! items.s: 'OPEN' YOUTHS RELAY — Oct. 20th. Report of Belgrave's open youths road relay on 20 October, won by Coventry in a close finish with Belgrave eighth; organised by Ray Conway (result on page 14). This year's race produced the closest finish yet---just 3 secs covering the first 3 teams, with Coventry moving from 5th to 1st on the last stage; a race of great excitement for the many spectators. Nearly 40 teams faced the starter, and Leaver brought us to the first change-over in 14th place, ahead of Mitcham (18th) and only 10 secs behind Coventry (11th). John Bicourt then produced fastest time of the first two stages to take us up to third---what a great prospect this lad is!. Simmons ran his hardest against the class opposition but was forced to concede 5 places. "Noddy" Edwards ran his usual gutty race hanging on desperately to his 8th position in the final straight to bring the team home 93 secs behind the winners. The race was organised by Ray Conway, his first ever promotion, and it was a tribute to his fine work that a prominent Midland official should make an impromptu speech congratulating Belgrave on their excellent organisation. items.label: November 1962
items.sum: D.E.M.'s review of the disappointing 1962 track season, singling out Derek Boosey, Dereck Wade, John Thresher and Dave Cocks and thanking the officials.
items.s: Track Roundup D.E.M.'s review of the disappointing 1962 track season, singling out Derek Boosey, Dereck Wade, John Thresher and Dave Cocks and thanking the officials. We find ourselves at the end of the Track season and the first league cross-country matches already upon us. What can we say of the recent summer season? Essentially it has been another disappointing year with overall performances not being as bright as we had anticipated. As was to be expected, we are still lamentably short of real class field-events men and sprinters, although some indication was at last given, that youngsters in these branches of the sport are now doing very nicely. If we are to succeed, however, in the fierce competition of trophy matches, then we must be capable of producing a good all round, well balanced team and not rely upon our one and three milers to salvage some of the points. On the credit side, however, several athletes are worthy of mention. In particular are we proud to see Derek Boosey gaining international recognition and proving himself one of the top three triple jumpers in the country. Whilst on the subject of jumping, it is good to see Dereck Wade improving so consistently and indicating that he'll soon be reaching the 23' plus stage. Derek is a good all round sportsman and as he gains in strength and experience, he should prove himself the best Belgrave long-jumper ever. Let us also pay tribute to John Thresher, yet another of our truly home-grown athletes. John will run anywhere and in anything and his quiet approach conceals an intensely determined and dedicated individual. This year he exceeded all expectations, even, I suspect, his own and it was only fitting that he should carry off two titles in the Club Championships. Dave Cocks must surely be congratulated on his great form this year. His quarter-miling was remarkable for one who can be so good over the longer runs.(What other Brighton relay man can clock inside 50 for a lap?) Two Club records is good going for a season and the way he is moving they probably will not be his last. Finally, thanks to all those people who lent helping hands throughout the season. Those who held watches, pulled triggers and those who yelled down microphones. Let us hope that the coming winter will see some of the pure track athletes training twice a week instead of once and so make next track season the best for a long time. D.E.M. D.E.M. D.E.M. items.s: MAY 12th - EALING Report of the trophy match at Drayton Green, Ealing, on 12 May, where Belgrave were second on aggregate to Ealing, with David Cocks setting a junior 880 track record. The undersized track at Drayton Green is invariably in poor condition and consequently the record book shows few performances of note; although one can recall Bob Taylor clocking a 4:16.0 mile there when no more than ten runners in the land had broken 4:10.0. Nonetheless there is always an atmosphere of friendly competition and this is a fixture that is always enjoyable. The trophy was decided on the aggregate points score of Seniors, Juniors and Boys. The home club appeared to be the only one with any of the latter and this proved instrumental in their winning the contest, for their Seniors were last. David Cocks was in great form setting a track record for the Junior 880 with 1:59.3 - half a second faster than the Senior winner! Jack Hampshire (2:08.3) backed up well for 3rd place. The Junior mile was also a Belgrave party. Winner Alan Morrison (4:37.2) was followed by Steer (4:39.0) 3rd, Bicourt (4:40.0)-and still a Youth,- 4th, and Redwood, Angus and Satchell making it 6 in 9. The short sprint was a blow for he-man Blumberg. He was an easy heat winner in 10.3 but in the final, pulled a muscle when excellently placed and hobbled across the line in 3rd position. Graham Worrell (24.2) and Pat Cornelius (24.8) were 3rd and 4th in the furlong, whilst Dave Mitchell (2:6.2) and F. Paget (2:12.0) took 5th and 7th places in the 880 yds. John Thresher and John Davies produced fine efforts to beat Barratt of Ealing in the mile clocking 4:24.4 and 4:25.7 respectively. As can be seen already, conditions were certainly not conducive to fast times. Bill Kerr ran a fine(9:25.0)2 miles to beat O'Gorman and Macey of St. Albans, but unfortunately we were short of a runner for the team race one good man could have swung both the Senior and total scores in our favour. However, we did win the medley relay and the result ended up as follows: Pos Team Points 1. St. Albans A.C. 26 2. Belgrave H. 24 3. Shaftesbury H. 17 4. Ealing H. 11 Pos Team Points 1. items.sum: Report and full results of the club track and field championships at Hurlingham on 26 May, with doubles for Graham Worrall, John Thresher and David Cocks.
items.s: CLUB CHAMPIONSHIPS Report and full results of the club track and field championships at Hurlingham on 26 May, with doubles for Graham Worrall, John Thresher and David Cocks. MAY 26th - HURLINGHAM. Inevitably performances generally suffered from the adverse weather conditions - a howling wind down the back straight and menacing overcast skies. We did have, however, certain bright athletic periods and the championships were supported by an unusually large number of athletes which seemed to indicate that there might be a resurgence of that old Belgrave spirit. We 'kicked off' with the 100 and this title went to Gerry Leroy, fresh from his annual winter lay-off, who had just a little too much pep for our old friend and former international star Alan Sexton. Alan is carrying a little more weight these days but it really is grand to see him on the track again. Later in the afternoon, Gerry, trying for the sprint double, made a perfect drop finish with inches separating the first four only to find that he had mistaken a post ten yards before the tape as the finish. This let in Graham Worrall and Pat (Nanny-Goat) Cornelius and Mike Smithers to take the medals. The 'quarter' developed into a two horse race between Worrall and Pete Pepe, whose form over the hurdles has of late been so encouraging. In the last few strides, however, Graham just had the edge and so took his second gold of the afternoon. It was notable that there were no standards gained in this event - shades of that epic final of 1959 when the last man clocked 51.3. Favourites often come unstuck and tipsters' faces are frequently red as they see their hottest tip floundering behind the leaders. Nobody would have given very long odds on John Thresher and sure enough, he lived up to his form by 'taking' John Davies down the finishing straight. All credit, though, to Dave Bains who took upon his shoulders the unwilling task of pacemaker. Stick to it Dave, one day they might not stay with you, remember Kuts in the 1954 European Games. John Thresher also annexed the mile title; it must have been about his slowest time of the season but it was the manner of his victory that was so impressive. Don Maclean had an unexpected 'good un' with Laurie O'Hara holding off clive Shippen for third place. In the Senior Field Events, we had our usual shortage of competitors, but this must in no way detract from the performances of young Derek Wade in the Long Jump. His jumping suggests that as he gains in strength and speed, he may well become another Percy Luxon and start challenging for top honours. The Junior Championships were,as expected, extremely well supported. Undoubtedly, the star was David Cocks who set up a championship 'best' in the 'quarter' and who also shrugged off all opposition in the 'half' to gain a double. The mile was something of a humdinger with Alan Morrison and Chris Steer battling all the way up the straight with Alan just getting the verdict and John Bicourt coming in well to take third place. No fewer than the first seven were inside standard time against six in the Senior event. It was encouraging to note that the 100 yards Boys Final was so well supported. Nelson just got the judges' decision from Archer on the tape with Condon in third place. Certainly the Club is weak in the sprints and these youngsters, given the right encouragement and training, could well put us back on the map. Style award. R. Barnes. Pos Name Perf 1. G. items.s: 13th JUNE - BATTERSEA Report of the senior and junior matches at Battersea on 13 June: the seniors second to South London Harriers, the juniors winning. Our main point-scorers in this match were Gerry Leroy, Bill Kerr, John Thresher and Pat Cornelius. Although beaten in the 220 yards by Marsh of Hercules, Gerry ran a fine 'quarter' to edge out Sunstan (S.L.H.) in 50.9 to show that he is still a force to be reckoned with over one lap. We also won the two mile team event, though even this fine team effort could not pull back sufficient points to wrest the match from S.L.H. RESULT 1. South London Harriers 71 points. | 3. Surrey Athletic Club 40 points. 2. Belgrave Harriers 68 points | 4. Hercules Athletic Club 35 points. JUNIORS With the really "big guns" giving this match a miss we had to look to our field events men for the points. Williams and Potlinger were more than equal to the occasion and won the Shot and Long Jump respectively. Roger Hudson also deserves credit for his 220 and 440 running. Without wishing to blow our own trumpets too much, this match went some way towards proving that we are Junior-wise, one of the top Clubs in the area. RESULT: 1. Belgrave Harriers 63 points | 3. items.s: 16th JUNE - CRICKLEFIELDS Short report of the poorly supported meeting at Cricklefields on 16 June, where John Thresher beat Bill Kerr in the mile. Although we did not seriously contest the team competitions some athletes emerged with flying colours. John Thresher and Bill Kerr fought out the mile with John getting home in 4:13:4 with our Scots laddie following in 4:14:8. Smithers and Leroy had a private battle in the Long Jump with Mike just beating his less experienced rival by the odd half-inch (19'6½" to 19'6"). Don Newell ran in the half and although obviously a little out of his depth he stuck to his guns right through to the tape. Poorly supported from the Belgrave viewpoint, this meeting nevertheless offered some good competition to those that did bother to attend. Wimbledon A.C. 42 points Leroy was our principal points-gatherer in this Belgrave victory - Gerry won the 440 yds in 51.8 and finished 3rd in the 100 yds (10.7). Worrall won the second string in 51.5 (probably 'niggled' at not being selected as No. 1.) Couzens won the Javelin (155'.1"), Kerr won the mile (4:18.1) and Mike Smithers popped up in several spots to collect valuable points. Special credit is due also to Derek Wade who, not only won the Long Jump (21'6½") but who also beat Mitcham star and former international Dave Brigden. This was a great club effort to beat two local rivals and also the strong Essex club. In a Junior match Mitcham proved too strong for us but all praise to Cocks for his win in the 440 (50.6) and for grand supporting roles played by Redwood (4:35·7) Mead (55.8), Morrison (2:2.1) and Pottinger (19'11½") in their respective events. The Youths forced a tie with Mitcham thanks largely to Bicourt (winning an excellent mile in 4:37.5) Peters, Martin and Miller. items.s: NORTH'S FIRST CLUB TITLE Report and result of the Club 3 miles on 25 July, won by Gerry North in a championship best 14:13.2. THE CLUB '3' - JULY 25th As was generally to be expected, Gerry North outclassed his opponents and leading from start to finish he established a best championship performance of 14:13.2. Although this was a time nowhere near Gerry's own personal best, the ease with which he smashed the existing record shows just how far we have to go as far as top-line competition goes. John Davies beat Don Maclean in a tussle for second place with O'Hara closing on them at the finish. The most encouraging feature of this event was the number of 'lesser lights' who got inside sixteen minutes and showed that we have certain strength in depth. Mention must also be made of young Bicourt who gave Chas Walker the fright of his life up the finishing straight! Pos Name Time 1. G. North 14:13.2 2. J. Davies 14:44.6 3. D. Maclean 14:48.0 4. items.label: November 1962
items.sum: Report of the match at Wimbledon Park on 1 August won by Belgrave, including Dave Cocks' club junior 880 yards best of 1:56.4.
items.s: 1st AUGUST - WIMBLEDON PARK Report of the match at Wimbledon Park on 1 August won by Belgrave, including Dave Cocks' club junior 880 yards best of 1:56.4. 1. Belgrave Harriers 148 points 2. Wimbledon A.C. 121 points 3. Sutton & Cheam H. 52 points Our lads seem to like this track for they always turn out in force at this fixture. Indeed so many claret and gold vests were in evidence that we practically swamped the senior half and mile events. O'Hara and Maclean finished first and second in the mile with two youngsters Fairclough and Bicourt fighting it out for fourth and fifth places to clock 4:31.0 and 4:32.0 respectively. In the half mile Paul Ellis of Poly had the legs of John Thresher in the straight but Pete Pepe slipped nicely to third spot to help with the points situation. Whilst talking of half miling we must congratulate Dave Cocks on setting up a new club Junior best of 1:56.4 - a performance which whilst it seemed inevitable, does erase from the book one of the most long-standing club records set up almost ten years ago by Frank Wright. Another heartening feature of this match was that we at last won the relays - the Seniors finished in 45.7 and Juniors in 46.9. Certainly if we all supported our matches as we did this one, then we would certainly be well on the way back to being a major athletic force. The talent is obviously there, so let's give it a little more airing! items.sum: Report and result of the Club 6 miles track championship at Battersea, won easily by Ron Linstead for the Tom Carter Cup.
items.s: THE CLUB '6' Report and result of the Club 6 miles track championship at Battersea, won easily by Ron Linstead for the Tom Carter Cup. "EASY WIN FOR LINSTEAD" "Fresh" from his South African exploits over 53 miles of hard undulating road, Ron Linstead showed that a mere 6 on a level track at Battersea was really quite a cake-walk by beating Pat Newell and Barry Sawyer by 120 yards and 180 yards respectively and so now holds the 'Tom Carter Cup' for this event. Shippen led the field through three laps with Walker taking over for another two, and at three miles this pair, with Linstead, Sawyer and Newell had broken clear of the field. On nearing the 3 miles time of 15:18, Linstead raced ahead and soon opened up a considerable gap. Although this was reduced a little in the closing stages, he was a comfortable winner and had run his last three miles only 2 secs slower than his first. Pat Newell ran very well in his first race for many months to gain second place and Barry Sawyer, despite not being in full training, took the bronze. That promising fledgling Archie Bedford, still only 44 years old, turned in a brisk 32:51 to get amongst the standard medals once more. Of the 23 starters, 20 finished. Pat Parker was placed third in the 3 miles (14:28.0) and earned selection against France the following week. items.sum: M.F.J.'s review of the field events section's season, highlighting Derek Boosey's international triple jumping and junior Dereck Wade's records, with a ranking list and a shot-put cartoon.
items.s: FIELD EVENTS Review M.F.J.'s review of the field events section's season, highlighting Derek Boosey's international triple jumping and junior Dereck Wade's records, with a ranking list and a shot-put cartoon. I review the past season's efforts by the field events section with mixed feelings. There have been some good individual performances, but when it came to combined efforts in Trophy meetings, our efforts were rather poor. At our open field events meeting only two Bels turned out to compete; Dave Wiseman was 5th in the Lomg Jump 18'6" and H. Leyer 5th in the Javelin with a throw of 161'1". In the Club championships also it was noticeable that with the exception of a few, the general standard was lower than the track section. The first Trophy meeting of the season was the "Vancouver Trophy" at Woodford Bridge. Derek Boosey won the triple jump and George Edwards was placed 4th in the hammer. Two months later at Wimbledon, H.H.H. promoted their "Brockman Trophy" and only two Bels turned out, Derek Boosey and Bill Couzens. Derek won the triple jump and Bill came 7th in the javelin. At Chiswick the following week we entered a team for the "Sward"; we finished last out of 12 clubs with 6 points. Derek Wade did well in gaining points in the long jump and high jump and he also competed in the triple jump. Bill Couzens was unlucky in not getting to the final six in the javelin. Peter Pepe finished 4th in the 440 yards Hurdles. Basil Blumberg who has been troubled with an injury, got into the final of the 220 yards hurdles but did not finish due to a recurrence of this. When taking the water jump in the 3 kilometres steeplechase, Alan Black fell and injured himself, later x-rays showed that he had fractured a bone in his leg. Alan who has been running well this season, came third in the steeplechase at the Scottish Championships in a new club record of 9 minutes 20 seconds, a few weeks earlier. A fast time in one of the big races may have got him a place in Scotlands Empire Games team at Perth. Of all the performances this season undoubtedly the best has been put up by Derek Boosey in the triple jump. In his first season with the Bels he has gained an A.A.A. vest,represented the Northern Counties, R.A.F. and the Combined Services, he was reserve for Great Britain in the match against Poland and then represented England against Finland. At the White City in the A.A.A. championships he was 4th in the triple jump with a distance of 50'6". Dereck Wade was the most outstanding performer among our juniors. Dereck equalled the Club junior record for the high jump with a height of 5'8" at the Club championships, he also won the senior long jump with a distance of 21'11" beating the existing Junior record of 21'6½" held by F. Skelley which was set up as long ago as 1957. At the L.A.C. Schools, Dereck was 4th in the long jump. As London schools champion he represented London at the All England Schools championships at Hull. With a faster "run up" which I am sure will come, he should be jumping well over the 23 ft. mark. items.sum: Walking section review of the 1962 summer: Ray Hall and Ray Middleton's European selection, Hall's sub-8-hour Stock Exchange London to Brighton, George Williams turning to running, new members, and results of club and county walks.
items.s: WALKING Walking section review of the 1962 summer: Ray Hall and Ray Middleton's European selection, Hall's sub-8-hour Stock Exchange London to Brighton, George Williams turning to running, new members, and results of club and county walks. Our two Rays of sunshine, Hall and Middleton, have certainly turned on the heat this summer. Their second and third places in the National 50 Kilos at Luton behind Olypic gold medallist Don Thompson was great stuff and earned them well-deserved places in Britain's European Games team for Belgrade. Ray Hall's magnificent win in the Stock Exchange London to Brighton walk earned him a headline of his own in the "News of the World" (back page of course!) "Record Walk for Ray (28)" glared the heading, but the write-up didn't mention that his time of 7 hours 58 minutes and 33 seconds had enabled him to enter that very select band of walkers who have beaten 8 hours for this journey. These are, Harold Whitlock, Don Thompson, Tom Misson and now Ray Hall Three of them have represented Great Britain in Olympic and European Games - two winning titles in the Olympics, and the third winning important International walks abroad. We wish number 4 on the list good fortune and the opportunity of proving himself the equal of those other three distinguished men. George Williams began the season in terrific form with several fast 2 mile times and looked a strong candidate for the European Games, but George had the misfortune to be 'pulled' on a couple of occasions and was considerably disheartened as a result. So much so that he turned to running, and within a matter of weeks ran in Belgrave colours for the Surrey Road Relay race, and was eventually nominated for the Club team in the classic London-Brighton Relay. Whichever section George may choose to perform in - who knows it might be field events next - the Club can always be sure that in this stalwart Bournemouth-based athlete, it has a true Belgravian. If the walking ranks appear poorer for the loss of George, they are certainly richer by the addition of Vaughan Thomas. Although in need of more coaching he has already made his mark in open competition. Vaughan, who is in the R.A.F., is a basket-ball international and can be seen at walking events sporting his "Great Britain" track suit - he could well become the first duo-international at these sports. We are pleased to welcome to our ranks all newly joined men and in particular we would mention 20 year old Dave King who hails from Bournemouth. Dave is another great prospect whose keeness to do well is illustrated by his desire to join us from such long range. Unfortunately, we must wait 14 months (from last July) before he can represent us in open competition, but he will no doubt make good use of this period to gain experience he will surely need for our first teams. items.label: November 1962
items.sum: Alf Harley's report of the R.W.A. 20 miles walking championship at Birmingham on 12 May, where Belgrave were third team and retained the Nijmegen Shield for the eighth successive time; Ken Matthews won.
items.s: THE R.W.A. '20' Alf Harley's report of the R.W.A. 20 miles walking championship at Birmingham on 12 May, where Belgrave were third team and retained the Nijmegen Shield for the eighth successive time; Ken Matthews won. Alf Harley reports:— We travelled to Birmingham on May 12th feeling that if all went well we could even win this Championship once again. As it happened we gained third place by the margin of one point only; but our strength in depth prevailed once again and we retained the NIJMEGEN Shield for complete teams of eight. It was a cold uninviting day over the two lap course which was plagued with traffic in parts, but the walkers found it to their liking and a tremendous number finished inside first-class standard time. From the start the holders Sheffield United Harriers swept into the lead with an impressive flurry of red and white hoops, and there they stayed until the last testing three miles revealed their weaknesses. Our lads in the early stages seemed set for a good show. Ray Middleton was walking with good judgment, the two Halls seemed to have settled down to a steady companionable race and Bob Barnes, after rather too fast a start, still looked a reliable fourth man. As the race developed, Middleton came through well picking up a number of places but was unable to break through into the first three. Ray Hall, walking the last few miles as fast as anyone in the race, picked up point after point - truly a Captain's effort. Eric Hall, however, had an off-day and found the last miles long ones indeed, but he kept going and was our third man home. Don Bartliff had taken over fourth team position for us, and confirmed that he has all the promise of championships to come in the years ahead; well backed by Ken Bailey, George Beecham, and Will Belderson. John Keown and J. Morris followed our eighth man in closely, and with Bernard Eglinton and Harry Shields completed our 'B' team. Meanwhile Ken Mathews had recorded an easy win having led from start to finish in his first 20 miles Championship, pursued by Don Thompson the holder. Before the race our Walking Hon. Secretary and Captain had the extremely difficult task of selecting our team of eight. As Ray Hall said, we would like to "perm eight out of ten" but it must go on record that the nominated eight were, in fact, our first eight to finish - which surprised even our Officers! In truth, we finished ten men before any other Clubs' eight - a magnificent performance. Our team gained the Nijmegen Shield for the eighth successive occasion; and each time our former Captain George Beecham has been in the team - a truly splendid personal record. Altogether we have recorded 14 wins in this Shield competition in 28 events. Coming back to the Championship, Surrey Walking Club with a fancied four, came through in the closing stages of the race to win their first Championship since 1948; and we congratulate them most heartily. Sheffield the holders, lost valuable places near the end but held on to second team position; and as previously indicated we were placed third. Leicester had hopes of those third medals but the one point margin was in our favour. We have now been placed in all the 20 mile Championships held since the War, seventeen consecutive placings, five of them wins. Going back to pre-War Championships our record is 24 consecutive placings to date. In fact since we were first placed in this Championship in 1922 we have only been unplaced three times in 34 competitions, winning the Championship eleven times All this is indicative of good team work, mutual support and good leadership; and without taking anything away from the excellent Captains we have had in the past, we can say that Ray Hall is the best yet, and that his influence and example will be seen in our teams for many years to come. items.sum: Report of the R.W.A. 50 km championship at Luton on 23 June, won by Don Thompson for the seventh time with Ray Middleton second and Ray Hall third; Belgrave second team and winners of the new Milan Trophy.
items.s: THE R.W.A. 50 Kilos Report of the R.W.A. 50 km championship at Luton on 23 June, won by Don Thompson for the seventh time with Ray Middleton second and Ray Hall third; Belgrave second team and winners of the new Milan Trophy. This year's race was held on a very fine 2 lap course from the Vauxhall Motors Ground, Luton, on June 23rd. Although Don Thompson gained his 7th successive 50 kilos victory he did not have it all his own way. From the 25 Km. mark to that at 40 Km. Ray Middleton pushed the Champion very hard and Thompson was very pleased to finish. Ray finished an easy 2nd with the excellent time of 4:30.59. After a fast start Thompson reached the 10 Km mark 2½ minutes ahead of the field! Ray Middleton and Vaughan Thomas (!) were chasing hard amongst the leading challengers, with Ray Hall backing up well. At 25 Km. Middleton had left the field well behind and was a mere 8 secs. down on Thompson. The battle was on! As hard as Ray tried, it took a full 5 Km. to pare off another 2 secs. but 10 Km. later the gap had stretched to 24 secs. - after 3½ hours of walking! Ray's effort eventually took its toll and he was forced to ease and be content with 2nd place, a truly great effort. Ten minutes or so behind the field was battling it out and, with a nicely paced effort, Ray Hall worked his way through to gain a fine 3rd place. The team race was extremely close and we were forced to relinquish our hold on the Trophy by the narrow margin of 2 points. Surrey W.C. were the victors with some excellent packing. However, the Bels won the newly instituted "Milan" Trophy for the first team to finish 8 men ( 8 in 28) so all in all, it was a good day for the Club. (95 started) Teams. 1. Surrey W.C. items.s: JULY/AUGUST Walking notes for July and August: the annual inter-club walks at Battersea with a Japanese guest team, club handicaps and Ray Middleton's fifth in the A.A.A. 2 miles. At our annual inter-Club Walks at Battersea on July 4th we had a guest team of 3 Japanese Walkers taking part in the 5 miles event and a small presentation was made to them afterwards by the President. Seventy-five Walkers took part in the 4 races and 11 teams finished. Surrey W.C. were the victors (157 pts.) after another tight finish. Met. W.C. (155 pts) and Woodford (154) were 2nd and 3rd with ourselves 4th (144). D. Bartliff and H. Shields were 16th and 18th in the '5', R. Middleton and W. Belderson 2nd and 7th in the '4', J. Knifton and H. McGreechan 6th and 12th in the '3' and R. Barnes and G. Cameron 6th and 11th in the '2'. Ray Middleton recorded a fast 14:30 2 miles in a Club Handicap on July 9th to beat Bob Barnes by 47 secs. HANDICAP RESULT: 1. G. Cameron (3:10) 13:24 3. R. Middleton (0.55) 13:35 2. R. items.label: November 1962
items.sum: D.E.M.'s report of the club's annual general meeting on 20 September 1962: honours boards from Ken O'Kell, a subscription increase, Sid Roberts' retirement as Treasurer, Dave Shepherd elected President and Gerry North cross-country captain, honours badges and Arthur Penstone's life membership.
items.s: A.G.M. 1962 D.E.M.'s report of the club's annual general meeting on 20 September 1962: honours boards from Ken O'Kell, a subscription increase, Sid Roberts' retirement as Treasurer, Dave Shepherd elected President and Gerry North cross-country captain, honours badges and Arthur Penstone's life membership. THURSDAY SEPTEMBER 20th. Like the Club Dinner, the A.G.M. seems to act as a magnet for all true Belgravians. Although the Hall was not filled to capacity, there was in attendance the best part of a hundred faces, young and old, the familiar and the almost forgotten, all intent upon the business in hand, namely the administration of Belgrave affairs. After the usual pleasantries and, in some cases, reunions, we got down to 'brass tacks! We were introduced, many of us for the first time, to Ken O'Kell, a past President of the Club and a man with a genuine and fond affection for the Belgrave Harriers. Ken was present largely for the purpose of handing over to the Club two honours boards, one recording Past Presidents, the other, International Athletes. These Boards, one of which is already in place, are to grace the walls of our Headquarters giving us a visual record of many notable members. They were duly presented, and their donor made an excellent speech which revealed not only something of his life with Belgrave, but also his pride in being a member of the Club. Next on the agenda came the presentation of our financial position by our own financial wizard, Sid Roberts. Although we are still keeping our head fairly well above water, it was emphasised that we are becoming increasingly subsidised by football competitions and schemes of similar form . It was indeed largely on account of this that a motion was later to be proposed,and passed,by the meeting to the effect that subscriptions should be raised to 30/-d. in the case of Seniors and to 15/-d. in that of Juniors. Although the voting on this motion was by no means unanimous, it was generally felt that such an increase would in some measure lessen our dependence upon income from outside sources such as football schemes. The Treasurer's report itself was something of a sad affair, inasmuch as it marked the end of some ten years service by Sid Roberts in that somewhat unenviable position. Unfortunately, business ties have called Sid away from office, but we are sure that all Belgravians would agree that a hearty vote of thanks is due to him for the tireless and sincere way in which he has performed his duties. The greater part of the meeting was taken up with the election of Club officers and whilst there was the usual spate of 'no changes', we must mention certain elections, not out of mere courtesy, but because they are offices which greatly affect us as a Club. First and foremost, of course, Dave Martin Shepherd was elected President (another bald 'un). Dave of course, is a great personality and if he can spread just a little of his own enthusiasm throughout Belgrave, his year of office can hardly fail to be successful As if this role was not sufficient, he was later made Treasurer, so it looks as if we're on our way to a dictatorship! At this juncture, we must also say 'thank you' to Arthur 'Nutty' Penny for the way he has filled the Presidency over the past twelve months. Certainly it can be said that during the past year there has been a stirring of the old 'Bels' spirit, let's hope this really bursts into life under Dave Martin. Another election of interest was that of Gerry North, National Cross-Country Champion, to captaincy of the Country Section. His qualifications, of course, are insurpassable and during the brief time that he has been with us he has shown that he holds the interests of Belgrave strongly at heart. Certainly if our boys back him up, even make him fight for his place in the teams, then there is no reason why we shouldn't be challenging for championship honours once again. It is customary during the A.G.M. for Honours Badges to be presented, and this year these were awarded to David Cocks, John Thresher, Gerry North, Derek Boosey and Derek Wade (Junior). Particular mention ought to be made of the fact that Cocks has gained his Senior bedge whilst a Junior and also his Junior Standard whilst only a Youth. At this stage too, the Boys and Youths medal competition awards were made to P. Smith and R. Dommett respectively. A proposal made by Dave Martin Shepherd and seconded by Pat Cornelius that Arthur Penstone be elected to Life Membership was carried unanimously. This comes as a fitting reward to Arthur who, in addition to his activities in relation to the Road Running section, has also contributed considerably to the maintenance of Belgrave Hall. After a final vote of thanks to Sid Roberts, voiced by Colin Collis, the meeting was adjourned. It is reported in some quarters, that Dave Martin Shepherd was in fact, last seen buying 'halves' all round. D.E.M. D.E.M. D.E.M. items.s: ROAD RELAYS: SURREY Co. ROAD RELAY Report of the Surrey County road relay on 8 September, where Belgrave were third, with John Thresher fastest of the day and walker George Williams making his running relay debut. September 8th - We usually experience some difficulty in raising a fully representative team for this event owing to holidays but this year our strength was more befitting the Club and for the first time for many years we secured 3rd place thanks largely to an excellent run by John Thresher on the 5th leg, who with 13:51 put up the fastest time of the day. Eric Gebbett our first leg specialist brought us into 8th place just over ½ minute behind Barry Collins who gave Surrey A.C. a lead which they soon lost,never to regain. The 2nd leg was taken by George Williams better known in top class walking circles. This was George's first competitive relay run and performing like a veteran, he took us up one place and brought us 6 secs. nearer the leaders (Walton). Next to run was Chris Steer, one of our most promising Juniors. Chris ran a good leg, gaining another place but losing some ground on Walton, who had gone well ahead through a fast run by Bob Roath. Charlie Walker gained 10 secs. on the leaders and brought us to 4th place with a typically solid effort on the 4th stage. John Thresher, fresh from an excellent track season in which he had produced a number of sub 4:10 miles, proved that his basic speed was also suitable to road running and with the fastest time of the day put us into third place within sight of the leaders, Walton and Herne Hill. Don Maclean who has been running far more consistently of late, pulled out all the stops in an effort to pull back the two Clubs ahead, but to no avail and we had to be content with 3rd position. items.sum: Report of the Polytechnic road relay, where Belgrave beat Poly, T.V.H. and Walton but finished second to Portsmouth; Gerry North broke the course record and the 'B' team won medals.
items.s: BELS. THWARTED IN POLY. RELAY Report of the Polytechnic road relay, where Belgrave beat Poly, T.V.H. and Walton but finished second to Portsmouth; Gerry North broke the course record and the 'B' team won medals. For many years now our main rivals in this event have been the promoting club Polytechnic Harriers, with T.V.H. and Walton A.C. also great dangers. We had never yet been able to conquer all three at once - yet this year we did it! Why didn't we win then? Well the strongest club in the South decided to enter for the first time - yes, Portsmouth A.C, and they must be given full credit for their win, for they succeeded without the inseparable Hyman/Tulloh partnership, who were performing great feats in Belgrade. So the Bels were destined for second place again, although the 'B' team took winning 'B' medals for the 4th time in 7 years. Eric Gebbett (A) Jack Brown (B) and Ray Conway (C) set off on the first stage and eyebrows were raised when Jack and Eric came down the finishing straight together in 6th and 7th positions - a fine start for both teams. Charlie Walker ran well to take the 'A' team up to 4th and handed to our new 'star' John Thresher. John's fast miling this year has made him a little impetuous at the start of these longer runs and within a mile he had taken the lead. He had to give way eventually to Woodford's Willie Heiburg but still turned in an excellent 13:12. John Moore had a steady run and Ron Linstead and Barry Sawyer consolidated our position amongst the leading four. Gerry North then took over for the penultimate stage and showed everyone what a great road-runner he is by smashing Hogan's course record by 9 seconds, to record a fantastic 12:38. Even so, Portsmouth were still out of reach and Don Maclean only had to go through the formality of maintaining our comfortable second spot. Jack Brown and John Davies were our fastest 'B' men, but special mention should be made of young Tony Fairclough, who recorded an excellent 14:05 and of Cyril Forey whose 13:59 for the 'C' team may have seemed bad selection - in fact he had been in training for but 3 weeks after a 5 month lay off and showed everyone once more what great natural ability he possesses. We closed in three complete teams. Day's fastest. 1. North (Bels) 12:38 2. Heiberg (W.G) 12:54 3. Salvat (Port) 13:03 Pos Team Time 1. Portsmouth A.C. 106.39 2. Belgrave H."A" 107.58 3.
