items.sum: Report and result of the Blackpool and Fylde Memorial Road Relay on 24 April, retained by Belgrave from Manchester & District Lads Club.
items.s: 6th Annual Blackpool and Fylde Memorial Road Relay Race Report and result of the Blackpool and Fylde Memorial Road Relay on 24 April, retained by Belgrave from Manchester & District Lads Club. April 24th 1965 Two teams (less one last minute defaulter) journeyed by road to Blackpool on the day before the race and were accomodated in North Shore boarding establishments. We were the holders of the trophy, said to be worth 300 guineas, and a very strong team was never in danger of losing the race, although at the finish Manchester & District Lads Club had closed a lead which at one time was as much as 90secs to a mere 40 seconds. John Thresher took the first leg for the A team with Mel Thorpe running for the B team. John gained a ten seconds lead over Manchester & District Lads Club with Mel third about 200 yards behind. On the second stage Gerry North opened the gap to about fifty seconds and John Dear held on to 3rd place for the B team. Trevor Hart ran the third stage for the A team and widened the gap over the Manchester club to about 80 seconds but Bolton United who had had a bad start had moved into 3rd place with a fast run by Freary who with 21:53 put up a new record for the course. The B team, with an unfit Peter Hilliar running, were falling back. Tony Fairclough took the fourth leg and kept the lead but Brian Hall of Manchester closed the gap to about thirty seconds and the Lads Club were getting confident of their chances. Geoff. North however, on leg five, soon altered the position by running away from Manchester and with only one leg to go our lead was about 80 seconds. Geoff. was in great form. Perhaps sharing a bed with Laurie O'Hara on Friday night had something to do with it! Laurie O'Hara made no mistake on the last leg and in fact lapped our B team (Chris Steer) in keeping us ahead--it is doubtful whether a faster finish has ever been seen on the Blackpool track. Manchester, with Entwistle had made a great effort to catch up and had reduced our lead to 40 seconds, though we were never in danger. After the race the boys (and the team manager) set out to enjoy themselves and were able to show the North brothers a thing or two about Blackpool which even they didn't know! In all a successful weekend for all concerned. Result A Team J. Thresher(22:24)Gerry North(22:8)T.Hart(23:6)A. Fairclough(23:27) Geoff. North(22:11)L'O'Hara(22:59). B Team R. items.label: August 1965
items.sum: Stage-by-stage report and result of the National London to Brighton Relay on 10 April 1965, where Belgrave finished fifth (level on time with fourth-placed Portsmouth) and Gerry North ran the fastest time of the day on stage 4, with E. Lacey's photograph of the finish.
items.s: Brighton Relay Stage-by-stage report and result of the National London to Brighton Relay on 10 April 1965, where Belgrave finished fifth (level on time with fourth-placed Portsmouth) and Gerry North ran the fastest time of the day on stage 4, with E. Lacey's photograph of the finish. April 10th 1965 Our selected team for this race was probably the strongest that we had ever fielded and on this fact alone we were justified in hoping that we would finish higher than our fourth place in 1964. Unfortunately we found our main opposition at the top of their form with one team, North Staffs & Stone, running far ahead of their previous best. Our finishing position of fifth was by no means a disgrace, and was in fact, broadly speaking, a better performance than in 1964,for we were only 2½ minutes behind the winners instead of over 6 minutes. This means that whilst we are improving, teams like Coventry and Derby may well have passed their peak and we can look forward to 1966 with great anticipation. Laurie O'Hara on stage 1 did all that we had expected of him--he gave us the lead we needed and sent off John Thresher on what we had hoped would have produced a good margin by the time Mitcham was reached. Stage 2 has, however, given John a complex--although he is probably our third best runner over five or six miles he wont believe it himself and his performances suffer in consequence. Instead of romping away from the opposition he was forced to drop back to fifth and we were 30 seconds in arrears when Pat Newell took over heading for Wallington. Pat also lost a little ground with a run somewhat below that which we had expected after his excellent effort in the club 5¾. Gerry North running on stage 4, one of the hardest of the whole race, was in devastating form. From seventh to second against strong runners was a first class performance. To take 37 seconds off John Cooke of Portsmouth and to record the fastest time of the day, even with Ron Hill on the leg, was better than even his most ardent supporters would have expected. Trevor Hart ran well on the Redhill stage and kept his place, although losing a little ground on Coventry, and when Jack Brown (40 this year!) took over on the short leg Coventry were only 37 seconds ahead. Jack reduced this lead to 22 seconds and sent off Mel Thorpe with every chance of going into the lead. Mel made no mistake, and producing almost the carbon copy of an earlier race when Laurie O'Hara took this stage, came home with fifteen seconds to spare. Geoff North came next on the most gruelling leg of them all and fought every inch of the way, but Dominic Keily of Derby and Dick Taylor of Coventry were in great form and at Handcross we were back to third, but only ten seconds behind Derby and two behind Coventry. Could Bill Kerr keep close enough to Kilby and Bullivant to give our last three runners a chance or would these top class runners open up a large gap? The latter ,not unexpectedly, proved to be the case and John Jackson, running for North Staffs, caught up forty seconds and also put a long distance between himself and Bill. At the start of stage 10 we were fourth and nearly two minutes down on Coventry who were only a short distance ahead of Derby. Charlie Dabbs obviously thought there was still hope of a place for he gained sixteen seconds on North Staffs and 22 seconds on Coventry, although losing a few yards to Derby. The gaps behind were closing. Portsmouth who had been behind us for some time were getting ominously near, for Meadows on this leg put up the best time of the day,and were at this point a mere nineteen seconds behind us. Tony Fairclough, who had run so well on the Dale Hill stage last October, was well below his usual form and instead of repeating his previous effort he lost much ground and a place to Tim Johnston of Portsmouth who proved to be his club's ace card. And so to the last leg which Alan Black was taking. We were not really worried about being 30 seconds down on Portsmouth for we were sure that Alan would catch Gough. This he did and Alan was with the Portsmouth runner with a mile to go. Knowing Alan's fast finish we were still confident but Gough hung on and in a desperate effort, which some athletes seem to be able to produce even when they are on their knees, came home by inches from a most surprised Black. In front another battle had been enacted between Coventry and Derby--Coventry turning a small deficit into a winning lead of fourteen seconds to win for the third year in succession after a race which had proved to be one of the best contested for many years. items.sum: Cross Country Secretary's reminder of the News of the World's rules for supporters and runners in the Brighton Relay.
items.s: Cross Country Secretary's Footnote Cross Country Secretary's reminder of the News of the World's rules for supporters and runners in the Brighton Relay. I would like to take this opportunity of bringing to the notice of all members a number of conditions applied by the "News of the World" to Brighton Relay Races. As most of you know there is now to be only one race each year and if this is to be continued it is imperative that the rules are observed. I am therefore setting out below the conditions which in the past I have noticed are not observed by many of our members. 1. No supporters vehicles may follow the race on the first two stages. 2. Owing to the narrow roads on Stage 3 supporters' vehicles must not follow the runners through Wallington. 3. Runners must travel in the official coaches until they have run their stage of the race.. 4. No runners may run on the road except on their allotted stage. The police give permission for the race to be run on the understanding that there are no more than 20 runners on the road at any one time. Supporters must not run with the race, and runners in the race must not continue beyond their allotted stage. Failure to comply with these requirements may bring about the Club's exclusion from future races. London to Brighton Road Relay Wallington

items.sum: Evelyn Stimpson's account of the club's Butlins weekend at Bognor organised by Charlie Manning.
items.s: SOCIAL: The Butlins Weekend Evelyn Stimpson's account of the club's Butlins weekend at Bognor organised by Charlie Manning. The convoy to Bognor for the Butlins weekend,made their rendezvous on the Friday evening at the "Bels Hut" to wait for the arrival of our President and his wife. After a quick drink and a game of darts we were on our way,twice managing to lose our Social Sec.(C.Manning)in the space of about six miles. The first time when his gear box decided to go wrong,and the second time on a building site,about which no questions shall be asked. We arrived at Butlins to a hot meal and warm comfortable chalets, and later spent the evening having a look round. For the next few days,in true Belgrave spirit,every single item of Billy Butlin's was tried and tested ; from the open fun-fair in the freezing cold,when Jack Goswell was nearly robbed of his false teeth while tearing around on the "octopus" ,to all the fun and games which would have been nothing without the Harriers all doing their sprints around the dance hall and winning most of the prizes. The heated swimming pool was warmly appreciated by all,tempting even the chilliest mortals amongst us. Perhaps it was the warm water which made rather strange happenings occur to Jean Manning while swimming. But who can be surprised when the swimmers around her happen to be Dave Shepherd, Ted Stimpson and Jean's "Ole Man"? Butlin's bingo session and the local bookmaker accounted for some of the expenses of the party. Sunday afternoon our ladies turned up to a personality contest and much to their disappointment failed to win a week-end with a tall handsome "redcoat". The male members although not meeting with success in the knobbly knees contest were greatly appreciated by the audience in their rendering of the Swan Ballet. Dave making the best dying swan we have seen for a long time. We all departed on Sunday evening after a "restful" week-end,in general agreement that it had been most enjoyable,and we would like to express our gratitude to Charlie Manning for his hard work in organizing this trip. Evelyn Stimpson. items.label: August 1965
items.sum: Gordon Biscoe's account of the New Orleans jazz social at Belgrave Hall on 22 May with the Colin Bowden All Stars, organised by Charlie Manning.
items.s: JAZZ ON A SUMMERS NIGHT Gordon Biscoe's account of the New Orleans jazz social at Belgrave Hall on 22 May with the Colin Bowden All Stars, organised by Charlie Manning. The foundations of Belgrave Hall will surely never stand quite as firm since the night of May 22nd when those hallowed walls looked down on scenes of unprecedented transformation and frenzy. For this was the night when Charlie Manning climaxed his social triumphs of the year and brought New Orleans jazz to Denmark Road. From the attractively designed tickets this had promised to be something of an unusual social,and the subdued lights and decor showed that no effort had been spared to create the correct atmosphere. Anticipating the large crowd that was to gather,refreshment facilities had been doubled and these were soon operating at full stretch - eventually drying up. Charlie,from wise counsel and personal experience,had booked the'Colin Bowden All Stars' to complete the scene - musicians of professional standing such as Wally Fawkes and Jim Rogers. Whether one wished to dance or just listen,all tastes were catered for by the band's repertoire. While it is true that the Club's new 880y Champion had a job to convey his greatness above the noise,Bill Lucas's combination of speed and stamina on the dance floor spoke well of a come-back! The evening was finally brought to thunderous climax around 11pm to the apt strains of 'High Society' and everyone headed wearily for home,but not before a well deserved vote of thanks had been expressed to Charlie and his helpers for a truly great evening. May there be many more where that came from. items.sum: Walking section review: John Knifton leaving for Texas, new walkers David Mayo and Bill Newhill, absent members, hopes for the future, and Ray Middleton's National 50 km win and Lugano Cup selection, with R. Linstead's photograph of Thompson and Middleton.
items.s: WALKING Walking section review: John Knifton leaving for Texas, new walkers David Mayo and Bill Newhill, absent members, hopes for the future, and Ray Middleton's National 50 km win and Lugano Cup selection, with R. Linstead's photograph of Thompson and Middleton. The wheel of fortune forever turns. From our invincibility of a few years ago our rating is now just "strong opposition". It says much for the Club, of course, that despite a lean spell we still remain up amongst the medals. We have lost, or partially lost, several good walkers in recent years and we have been unable to replace them quick enough with new faces. A few weeks ago the position continued to worsen when John Knifton left these shores for Texas University to study for 3 years. John has been of great value to our teams over the years and we wish him the best of success in the U.S.A. New faces are badly needed and we are therefore very pleased to welcome 22yrs old David Mayo from the U.S.A. and 27yrs old William Newhill from Coventry. David was put on to Jack Goswell by Colin Young and after corresponding for a while he decided to come across here to get the competition he needs. How's that for keenness? Bill Newhill has already shown his worth wearing a Warwickshire vest and we look forward to these two finding a place in our teams. Eric Hall, who continues to support us at every opportunity, was very fit earlier this summer but went down with stomach trouble at a critical part of the season, and was unable to test his form over the longer distances once more. It would be a great boost for our teams if he could go out to 20 miles next season. Don Bartliff and Bill Belderson have both been posted elsewhere with the Police and we have seen little of them this year. Bob Barnes is now working in Cambridge and can only get down at weekends. Training packs from Belgrave Hall on Tuesday and Thursday evenings are not what they were a few years ago. Jack Goswell is convinced that our successes will return only when the packs reach their old numbers again. For the future, JWG hopes to see Steve Laker-Jones come on this winter and do well in next year's RWA 10 miles and 20 Kilos; also to see Pat Duncan and Dave King do especially well at the longer distances--they could be two of our main hopes next year. At the shorter distances Charlie Capener could also make good progress in 12 months. What a pity more of our walkers can't reach a peak for the National events like Ray Middleton. His ability to do this and his remarkable pace judgement are models to all athletes. After winning back his National 50 Kilos title from Nihill he is now rarin' to go in the Lugano Cup Final in Italy this October. items.label: August 1965
items.sum: Reprinted early-1950s training article by walker Jack Rutland on short- and long-distance walking training, followed by a note on his career.
items.s: HOW I TRAINED Reprinted early-1950s training article by walker Jack Rutland on short- and long-distance walking training, followed by a note on his career. We continue our series of training articles from Belgrave Newsletters of the early 1950's (3) JACK RUTLAND I started walking at the age of 15 years by winning the Bels one mile Novice event. It was not until two years later,however,that I was encouraged to enter 7 mile events. Whilst perhaps specialising in 7/10 mile events,at which reasonable success was acheived,first class standards have been gained at 20 miles and 50 kilometres, and I decided to make 1950 a long distance year. I believe that walkers can only expect good times by attaining real physical fitness;it is no good"taking a bashing" if you are not up to it. Therefore whether stripped training or strolling,make it regular and recover from one outing before attempting another. Improved times must be shown if physical fitness and style can be developed and from this should come stamina and speed respectively. As to the right amount of training,this will depend on the individual;I would say two or three times a week is sufficient,thus:- SHORT DISTANCE. Two mid-week outings and of course Saturdays club or race turnout.The distances mid-week can be restricted to 5/7 miles with time checks if possible. Strolling 10 miles on Sunday provided Saturday's outing has not been a hard race. LONG DISTANCE. Plenty of stripped spins 20/25 miles,with occasional"sharpeners" of 15/10 miles. Recovery is essential from each before attempting the next. Strolling once a week of 5 hours duration. I have found that stripped spins can score over strolls mainly because of time factors;more mileage can be covered to so build up confidence and knowledge of pace which is essential. One certainly needs to put in quite a lot of work for distance events, but providing a little is made,most walkers should be able to do some distance work and may find an increased strength the following season. Jack Rutland first made his presence felt by winning a club novice race at the age of 15 in the remarkably good time of 8:35. With increasing years he improved and was a member of our winning Junior team in 1936, finishing 7th. Following this he scored in many of our winning scratch teams in pre-war days. He won the first Army Road Walk Championship and in the season 1945/46 won a succession of open races in exemplary fashion. Thereafter he was Club Champion at 10 miles;Southern 7 miles Champion; second in the initial R.W.A. 10 mile Championship and placed in County Championships. Jack was among the six "possibles" for the Olympic Games 10,000 metres event in 1948 but did not strike his best form in that year. items.s: "Godstone" walk Note on the last Croydon to Godstone and back walk, where Dave King finished 8th. Dave King was our only walker of note to take part in the last "Godstone" walk, promoted by Surrey W.C. This Croydon to Godstone and back event covered a total distance of 18¾ miles and has been held annually since 1909. It is a pity we were not better represented on this farewell occasion. Dave King walked very well, and at halfway was 4th, only a few seconds behind M. Fullager and Selby. However, he paid the penalty for his fast start and dropped to 8th on the homeward journey clocking 2:52:32 against winner Nihill's 2:32:13. Dave King Dave King M. Fullager M. items.s: THE R.W.A. 20 kilos Report and result of the inaugural RWA 20 km road walking championship at Cardiff on 8 May, with Belgrave third team. 20 KILOS CHAMPS. CARDIFF---MAY 8TH The Race Walking Association's inaugural 20 Kilos road walking championship was held from Pontcalla Fields Cardiff, with 14 teams totalling 107 starters on the line. items.sum: Report and result of the RWA National 20 miles walk at Priest Hill, Ewell on 12 June, where Ray Middleton was second to Nihill but Belgrave were only 5th team, their worst National result for years.
items.s: R. W. A. National '20' Report and result of the RWA National 20 miles walk at Priest Hill, Ewell on 12 June, where Ray Middleton was second to Nihill but Belgrave were only 5th team, their worst National result for years. Poor Team Result for Bels This year's championship was held at the Priest Hill School Sports Centre, Ewell on June 12th. It is not a day Belgrave walking teams will wish to remember. To finish 5th of 11 teams in a National event is our worst performance for many many years. Even the loss of King, Barnes and Cameron during the race did not affect the result. In the individual race Ray Middleton walked exceptionally well and coming thro' in his usual style was only 43 seconds short of catching the winner, Nihill. Ray Hall was the only other Belgravian to gain a forward position. There were 110 starters. Norman Read, the 1960 Olympics 50 Kilo's gold-medallist, was first away and at 2 miles was 150 yards clear. At 5 miles Middleton had moved through to 4th place and shortly afterwards Read relinquished his lead to drop steadily back to 23rd. At the half-way mark Middleton was still 4th, nearly 3 minutes behind Nihill, and Ray Hall (14th) was having quite a battle with his old "Brighton" rival Dickie Green, Dave King followed close behind in 18th position, but it was not long afterwards that he suffered disqualification . With 5 miles to go, Middleton had moved up to second place, with Paddick (RSC) at his shoulder, and these two set their sights on Nihill whose lead had been reduced to 2½ minutes. The leader suffered a bad spell in the closing stages and although Ray dropped Paddick during his effort to catch Nihill he was still 43 seconds behind the Surrey walker at the line---a closeness that Nihill is not accustomed to these days! Ray Hall held his own throughout and finished strongly to beat both his race rivals, Green and Young. Barnes and Cameron retired in the closing stages. RESULT Pos Name Club Time 1. P. Bolton- 24th July We have a worthy National 50 Kilos champion in Ray Middleton. He walked a really well judged race to regain the title he lost to Nihill last year. Owing to holidays we could only start a depleted team, but Duncan, Beecham and Keown all walked extremely well to hlep earn us a 3rd place in the team championship--the title going, deservedly, to S.W.C. items.label: August 1965
items.sum: Clive Shippen's essay arguing that the amateur/professional distinction in athletics is illogical and that nationalism is a greater evil for the Olympic Games.
items.s: A DIRTY WORD ! Clive Shippen's essay arguing that the amateur/professional distinction in athletics is illogical and that nationalism is a greater evil for the Olympic Games. .......this is the reaction "professionalism" invariably gets. Are there too many heads firmly embedded in the sand? Are our interpretations of"amateur" and"professional" outmoded? Have we got our priorities wrong? ......Clive Shippen asks these questions and reviews the present illogical situation. The word AMATEUR is of french origin and stems from the latin words amator (lover) and amore (love). The professional sportsman,then,can be an amateur in spirit just as easily as the amateur can be a professional in approach. When some of the rowing clubs were first formed on the Thames, membership was restricted to "gentlemen" — to the exclusion of artisans. However one may view this sociologically, it was a fact that these "gentlemen" desired exercise with friends of similar physique and of similar occupation. A true amateur was one who gained no physical advantage from his daily occupation. If we leap across the years to the present day we find there is no restriction on an athlete who has a job,say,which necessitates a perfect shot-putting action being carried out fifty times a day;nor an athlete who has all day and every day to train while he is kept by his parents. Few people would argue that there should be any discrimination against these athletes - indeed,against any athlete - for the majority prefer to see the most able succeed,irrespective of how they obtained their prowess. It seems quite illogical therefore,that an outside and irrelevant factor should be introduced - "money",or in its broadest sense,"material gain". Not irrelevant? Then of what possible benefit could Arthur Rowe's rugby league football be to his shot-putting? Or Berwyn Jones's to his sprinting? Their participation in this tough game was a positive disadvantage to their athletics,with a fair risk of injury thrown in. As for the money they earned,well even if they used this to match the advantage of the "kept" amateur it would be to no avail,for they had already blackened their name with that dirty word "professional". So it is no longer a case of fair play,but a question of principle — just another rule,but with no evidence to support its existence. Let us suppose that monetary gain was not frowned upon and that sportsmen were judged purely on physical ability. Would Snell,Halberg,Clark and Co. start doing an extra 100 miles a week and go twice round the world each year instead of once? Would Eastern European athletes show vast improvements if they were paid broken time for all of the year? And would those swimmers who train six hours a day while their parents earn their keep suddenly acquire improved training schedules? Of course not. The attitude of leading athletes to material gain is purely incidental. If there is something to be had they'll have it - if not they'll train just as hard for the next race. Athletics is too tough a sport to enter just for the pickings - if any. If professionalism was given official blessing the most noticeable effect would be in the advertising field,as there is no money in athletic promotions. Our most famous athletes would be seen eating,drinking,wearing or using all manner of things. A few Olympic Gold Medallists might even be able to live on the revenue - as long as they stayed good enough. Athletic "purists" and opponents of material gain would be horrified to see such goings-on,but would it really do our sport any harm? Have the cycling and table-tennis worlds suffered? Surely the publicity would be beneficial , possibly resulting in higher attendances at the White City. Opponents of such licence should remember that for every athlete who thinks he can hold promoters,selectors or officials to ransom there are a hundred who would willingly pay to take his place. There are a handful of world famous names in any era whose crowd-pulling ability makes their owners potentially well off,but many a blind eye has already been turned towards the activities of some of these athletes in this so-called amateur age. Athletics administrators in all non-communist countries are,of course in a difficult position. To acknowledge even semi-professionalism (as cyclists have) would cut their country off from world competition until the others followed suit. No one,therefore,has the courage to take the lead in suggesting a revision to the rules. No one can be blamed, for such a suggestion would meet with violent opposition from the communist bloc,who do not recognise professionalism in any form,in theory; besides many other Western countries. Nationalism is already proving a far greater evil than professionalism Athletics enthusiasts form only a minute percentage of the multitude who eagerly await the gold medal tally at an Olympic Games. World interest is mainly concerned with National prestige and the resultant political propaganda and it is Nation versus Nation rather than athlete versus athlete. France is embarking on a mammoth programme to improve sports facilities, not because her sportsmen need them any more than before but because de Gaulle wasn't satisfied with the few medals gleaned at the last Olympics. China,in turn,will probably enter the Olympics when they consider their athletes (like their table-tennis players) are strong enough to beat the world. So the shades that appeared at the 1936 Olympics are continuing to darken. Rather than witch-hunt for technical "pro's" our administrators would do better to campaign for the abolishment of victory ceremonies and their nauseating crowd-chanting, flag-raising, anthem-singing embellishments; and make any other moves which will help to reduce the Nationalistic atmosphere of the Olympic Games. However, long after the Olympic Games has heaved its final death-throes and the amateur/professional wrangle is long forgotten,club athletics will still be pottering along very much in its present style. Scrubbers will still be wanting to run against scrubbers and stars against stars. Championships will still be held and life will continue to revolve round the domestic calendar of fixtures - and the only persons to have fallen by the wayside will be those who have forgotten that athletics is purely and simply contests of athletic ability between sportsmen who have not the slightest concern about the colour,class,creed or material gain of their opponents. Clive Shippen Clive Shippen Arthur Rowe Arthur Rowe Berwyn Jones Berwyn Jones Snell Snell Halberg Halberg Clark Clark de Gaulle de Gaulle Olympic Games 1936 Olympic Games 1964 Thames White City France China

Report and result of the 38 mile Hastings to Brighton walk on 14 August, where Belgrave took team bronze through Dave King and Ray Hall, and Pat Duncan travelled from France only to retire. How's this for keenness? Pat Duncan, on a working holiday in South France during his University vacation, and still in the throes of stomach upsets, insisted on driving from Toulouse to Dieppe, leaving his car at the port, taking the night ferry to Newhaven and travelling on to Hastings to represent the Bels in this year's 38 mile walk to Brighton. Unfortunately his mind was keener than his stomach and he was obliged to retire after 10 miles. No sooner was the race over than Pat was on his way back to Toulouse--quite an outing! George Beecham, who is currently coming into form again, was unable to start through a minor injury. However, thanks to Dave King and Ray Hall we were still able to get up amongst the medals. items.sum: Junior Section review of the 1965 track season, highlighting the junior sprint relay team coached by Ben Lulham, promising juniors and boys, and the work of Adrian Major and George Piddington.
items.s: Junior Section Junior Section review of the 1965 track season, highlighting the junior sprint relay team coached by Ben Lulham, promising juniors and boys, and the work of Adrian Major and George Piddington. With another track season nearly completed,we the Junior section can look back on a most interesting season,highlighted by the performances of the Junior sprint relay team coached to perfection by Ben Lulham. They took the Surrey 4 x 110y and 4 x 220y in best championship times and then won the Southern Counties 4 x 110y. They are now entered in the AAA's relays and I am sure we are in with a winning chance. The result,I hope,will be stop pressed in the 'Belgravian',this of course being written before the event. For those who are are not 'au fait' with the team,the regular members are:- Jim Vivian,Chris Martin,Denis Gleeson and Clive Oliver. Other juniors who have had a good season are John Mitchell,John Martin, Phil Smith,Bob Nelson,Dave Nicklin and Adrian Major. Many others who are under the guidance of Tom Carter are improving fast and the seniors will surely benefit in the very near future. Junior Track Captain,Adrian Major, has given the section invaluable service with his enthusiasm and drive and has helped to make my job much easier. Thanks a lot Adrian. We are well down in active Youth members,but the lads we do have are very keen. So seniors,if you know of any chaps who would like to join,we promise them some good sport and very good company. The Boy's department,membership-wise,is flourishing. Very good performances in the medal competition have shown potential,but this section,as always,is the hardest to hold together. Competition from schools of course has to be accepted,but other sports - Football and Rugby played on Saturdays,interferes with training and we are liable to lose touch. This is being overcome by the efforts of George Piddington and Adrian Major. One of our most promising boys J.Lewis,is one of the Football fans and I am told on good authority that he is a most excellent player. Another is J.Barnard who I know has been sought as a member by a number of prominent clubs. Jack Hampshire, Sen. Jack Hampshire Sen. Jack Hampshire, Sen. Parliament Hill Fields--March 6th JUNIOR: Our leading Junior of the winter, John Bicourt, had an excellent run to finish 22nd--a mere 13 seconds outside the first dozen and with only three Southern runners ahead of him. He was always in the first 30 and at one time reached 18th--a fine effort. The ever-reliable Jackie Hampshire was our next man (148) followed by Dave Cocks and Alan Morrison, both below their best. A disappointing points total of 673 gave us a lowly 28th team placing. RESULT 1. R. Taylor(Coventry) 2. I. McCafferty (Motherwell) 3. J. Hammond (Coventry) 22.J.Bicourt 148.J.Hampshire 208.D. items.label: August 1965
items.sum: George Piddington's report on the boys' coaching course of 2-3 April, and a note on young jumper Arnold Bent's ankle injury.
items.s: COACHING COURSE George Piddington's report on the boys' coaching course of 2-3 April, and a note on young jumper Arnold Bent's ankle injury. Sixteen boys attended the coaching course held on Friday evening and all day Saturday,April 2nd/3rd. Friday opened at the hall with an introductory talk on the Club's history by Charlie Jones followed by a short talk by our President. The rest of the evening was spent on the showing of loop films with comments by John Bromley,who not only had the keen interest of the boys,but the coaches also who learnt much. Saturday morning was spent again at the hall with a short talk on each event by the coaches. After a break for lunch everyone made their way to Tooting Bec track where the majority took an active part in most events. The weather could not have been better and conditions were ideal. I wish to convey my sincere thanks to all those who helped on this course and to Mrs Savage who arranged refreshments. Maybe there will be future stars in our ranks as a result of this coaching course - I hope so. We are sorry to hear of an injury to Arnold Bent who damaged his ankle whilst training at Battersea Park recently. Arnold,only 14½,shows great promise with a 19'0" long jump and a 5'1" high jump to his credit.On this particular occasion he cleared 20'0" for the first time in training. We wish him a speedy recovery. George Piddington George Piddington George Piddington Charlie Jones Charlie Jones John Bromley John Bromley Mrs Savage Mrs Savage Arnold Bent Arnold Bent Arnold Bent Arnold Tooting Bec track Battersea Park

April 23rd/24th - Motspur Park - L.A.C.Schools Meeting The LAC Schools meeting is renowned for high class performances,this year being no exception. John Mitchell once again won the Long Jump,only this time smashing the meeting record by 6" with a mark of 23'2". Such was his series of jumps that he beat the second man's distance four times. He followed this up in true Lynn Davies style by running a storming anchor leg in the relay to bring his team home first. The 100 yards produced a real blanket finish,Jim Vivian managing to get 3rd place with the same time as the winner - 10.3. May 15/16th - Wimbledon Park - PART 1 Our Junior relay squad - Oliver,Martin,Gleeson and Vivian - not only won both the County relays by the length of a street,but set new records in the process. Much of the credit must go to Ben Lulham under whose eagle eye these young athletes train. With a bit of luck and even slicker baton passes,the AAA Junior could come their way. Adrian Major ran well in the 2 miles to record a personal best of 9:38.2 . Badgery and Church,as expected,tore off into the lead,but Adrian ran a steadier race working his way through the field until just after the half-way mark he went into 3rd place which he held to the finish. 4x110y 1.BELGRAVE H 44.3 4x220y 1.BELGRAVE H 1:32.4 2m 3.A.Major 9:38.2 May 29th - Motspur Park - PART 2 The Youth 110y hurdles was won in a very good time by K.R.Finn. In clocking 14.8 (especially good considering the conditions) he qualifies for a Club Youth's Honours Badge. The Long Jump was a very close affair. Dave Nicklin improved 9" on his previous best with a leap of 20'9¾" to take 3rd place,only 4" covering the first three. In the absence of Jim Vivian (just out of hospital after an appendicitis operation) the Belgrave flag was still kept flying in the sprints with good efforts by Chris Martin and Denis Gleeson. items.s: CARSHALTON TROPHY (Junior)---31st July Report of the Carshalton Trophy junior meeting on 31 July, won by Belgrave, with John Mitchell's 23'2¾" long jump. After finishing 3rd in the 'A' 100 yds, Denis Gleeson was a convincing winner of the 'A' 440 yds, clocking 52.4. Jim Vivian was an easy winner of the'A' 220 yds (23.1) whilst John Mitchell clocked a very sharp 10.3 in the 'B' 100 yds. Outstanding performance of the meeting was undoubtedly John Mitchell's exceptional 23'-2¾" long jump win. It was good to see our Juniors clinch a trophy win by finishing up with a fine 6X220 relay victory. RESULT: 1. BELS 142 . 2. Brighton 120. 3.Mitcham 116. 4. Surrey 105. items.label: August 1965
items.sum: Chris Steer's report and full results of the club track and field championships at Hurlingham on 22 May, with club records for Nick Head (javelin) and Geoff North (880 yards).
items.s: CLUB CHAMPIONSHIPS Chris Steer's report and full results of the club track and field championships at Hurlingham on 22 May, with club records for Nick Head (javelin) and Geoff North (880 yards). May 22nd - Hurlingham The Club Championships were held on a cloudy but warm day which contrasts with the arctic conditions usually experienced at this meeting. Like the weather the standard of performances was not particularly high,often downright poor,although there were some occasional'bright periods' . Not surprisingly for Belgrave (how often must this have been said?) most of the better performances came in the Mile and Half,the only events where,it would seem,it would seem,there was any true depth. In the sprints and field events,although there were some excellent winning efforts,the overall standard was in many cases abysmally poor. An all time low must have been reached in the Senior 220 yards where only the winner could be said to have any real claims to being a sprinter. Time and again the achievments of the second and third places would have been a disgrace to a schoolboy meeting. However there were some performances worthy of note. One of the revelations was the casual ease with which Nick Head broke the Javelin record. From a run-up of a few yards he threw 207'7¾" - almost 20 feet further than Colin Clair's 1963 record. He also won the Shot and Discus with more modest marks. Another who demonstrated remarkable versatility was Clive Brooks who won the High Jump,Triple Jump,100 yards and 220 yards (another Gerry Leroy?). Completing the field events picture,Bob Jones jumped within 6" of the Long Jump record with 22'6½" . On the track the best race of the day was undoubtedly the 880 yards. It was a somewhat unusual line-up for a half - it would seem that certain middle distance runners can't bear to be separated from each other.Nevertheless, a fine race ensued with John Thresher making most of the running only to be outsprinted down the straight by(suprise! suprise!) Geoff North. The time of 1:56.3 broke Dave Cocks' record by one tenth of a second. John was second in the same time and Alan Morrison,showing a startling and welcome return to form,came third with 1:58.0 . The Mile provided some good performances but no-one could match Laurie O'hara's devastating finish. His time was an excellent 4:16.2 . Mel Thorpe (in great form these days) was second in 4:19.8 and Bill Kerr third in 4:20.2. The 3000m Steeplechase (a new championship event which should become more popular) proved an easy victory for John Bicourt whose experience at this type of race was too much for John Dear who had led in the early stages . The other senior track event,the 440 yards, was won by Alan Mead in 53.2 from a very sparse field. In the Junior events,Adrian Major found the 880/mile double too much for him - he won the mile in 4:47.0 but was beaten in the half by Richard Moody who recorded 2:07.3 . The junior sprints,unlike the senior were well supported and performances were good. Ben Lulham's 'stable' was well to the forefront in the absence of Jim Vivian (appendicitis) both 100y and 220y were won by Chris Martin with Denis Gleeson and C.Oliver second and third in both races. Other junior winners were R.Nelson (440y) and J.Martin (High Jump). In the Boys events winners were A.Bent (100y) and J.Lewis (880y). Generally then,a disappointing meeting especially for the handfull of spectators who did take the trouble to come. I may be biased,but it is time Belgrave stopped relying on the middle distance runners to provide all the excitement. However well they may run on the Brighton Road,they cannot win trophy meetings and the like. Perhaps with a solid nucleus of good junior sprinters and the few good field events men we do have,these Championships will be more worthy of the name of Belgrave in future years.Here's hoping. items.s: Geoff. North Strikes Again Report of the AAA v London University match at Motspur Park on 19 May, where Geoff North won the 2 miles in 8:43.0, John Thresher the mile, and John Mitchell became the first Belgrave junior to compete for the AAA. May 19th - Motspur Park AAA v London University On a chilly evening at Motspur Park,Geoff North confirmed his recent good form by winning the 2 miles in 8:43.0 from Mick Gowan 9:04.0,both representing the AAA. They shared the lead until with two laps to go when Geoff decided to clear out for home. Something in the 8:30's definitely looks possible from him this season. John Thresher,running in the mile,means business again this season. Never headed after halfway, he won by ten yards in 4:09.2. John Mitchell became the first junior Belgrave member to ever compete for the AAA on the field,finishing 2nd in the Long Jump to P.Reed (22'9¾" [?]) with 22'3½", and Dave Rees placed 4th in the Pole Vault for London University. items.sum: Note that Gerry and Geoff North have been chosen for a British Olympic Association altitude training trip to Mexico from 5 November.
items.s: FIREWORKS! ROCKETS! MEXICO! Note that Gerry and Geoff North have been chosen for a British Olympic Association altitude training trip to Mexico from 5 November. FIREWORKS! ROCKETS! MEXICO!-----"What is the connection"? you might ask. Well, on November 5th those North rockets, brothers Gerry and Geoff, will have their blue touch-papers lit at London Airport, will rise to about 20,000 feet, head W.S.W., and fall only a little over half that height to the land of the 1968 Olympic Games. Gerry and Geoff form part of a six man team of runners (others so far are M. Hyman, J. Cooke and D. Keily) who will be under the surveillance of Drs. Pugh and Owen and Chief Coach John Le Masurier during a one month's training programme in the rarefied atmosphere of Mexico. The trip has been orgainised by the British Olympic Association in order to ascertain the effects of altitude on the performances of distance runners and what sort of acclimatisation period is neccessary. items.s: SURREY Co. CHAMPIONSHIPS Report and results of the senior Surrey County Championships (Wimbledon Park 15-16 May; Motspur Park 29 May), where Gerry North won the 6 miles in a championship best and the 3 miles with a sprint finish, with R. Linstead's photograph. PART 1 May 15th/16th - Wimbledon Park Running entirely on his own from gun to tape,Gerry North had no trouble at all in winning his first Surrey Championship - the 6 miles. He lapped practically the whole field and broke the championship best performance by half a minute. 6m 1.Gerry North (BELGRAVE H)28.48.2 2.B.Collins (Surrey) 3.D.Holt (Hercules) 3000m Steeplechase 1.B.Collins (Surrey) 2.J.Bicourt (BELGRAVE H) 9:28.4 Photo : R.Linstead Gerry North leading the "Racing Holts", soon after the start of the Surrey '6' which he won in record time . SURREY CHAMPS continued PART 2 May 29th - Motspur Park Unfortunately the weather was not as kind as in recent years,an extremely cold wind blowing hard up the finishing straight. In the mile John Thresher was all out to improve on last year's second place,qualifying easily for the final with second fastest time. In the final he was rather slow away at the start but soon moved up towards the front where the Milner twins were doing their annual task of pace making. Normally taking off for home at the 'Elliott spot' (660y to go) John cannily waited until they hit the wind with just over a lap left. Unfortunately Tony Harris (Mitcham AC) hung on to him,finally overtaking in the finishing straight for a good win. Never mind John,third time lucky. The race of the day was undoubtedly the 3 miles in which Gerry North revealed a sprint finish nobody knew he had. With three-quarters of a mile to go Robinson (Cambridge) had shaken the whole field up by tearing away as if it was the last lap. He was 30 yards clear before anyone knew what had happened and didn't look like fading either. As the bell rang for the final lap Gerry slowly started to gain,but was still 25 yards down with only a furlong left. Then it happened. He streaked round the turn catching Robinson hand over fist. Belgrave supporters were in uproar for five yards from the tape they knew Gerry had got it. items.s: AN ENGLISHMAN ABROAD Report of the international 5000 metres in Paris on 11 June, won by Michel Jazy in a European record, with Geoff North 4th in 13:57.6. June 11th - Paris INTERNATIONAL 5000 Metres In his current form and with 30,000 screaming Frenchmen rooting for him, Michel Jazy just couldn't fail.Gamoudi of Tunisia was actually hissed by the crowd for not hanging on. Jazy has run a fantastic series of races lately and on this occasion broke the European Record,only missing Ron Clarke's world mark by a few yards. Geoff North finished 4th in his finest race to date with 13:57.6 (superior to his own Club 3 mile record by about 4 secs.). 1.M.Jazy(France)13:29.0 2.M.Gamoudi(Tunisia)13:44.2 4.Geoff North,13:57.6 Michel Jazy Michel Jazy Michel Jazy Jazy M.Jazy M. items.s: CECIL FRY TROPHY Report and results of the Cecil Fry Trophy meeting at Ilford on 26 June, where a weak Belgrave turnout finished 7th of 12 clubs and Mel Thorpe was 2nd in the 3 miles. June 26th - Ilford Although we had a very poor turnout we managed to finish 7th out of the 12 clubs taking part - it could be worse I suppose. All our team performed well but we had very few 2nd string men,so losing valuable points. Bill Kerr ran well in the 'A' mile,both he and Herring (Blackheath) closing on the leader in the last lap. Even with his final 'kick' Laurie O'Hara still couldn't catch Huffer (TVH) in the 'B' event,but once again he triumphed over his Blackheath rival John Baldwin. The 3 miles was an exciting race for after several laps of normal type pace,John "Maybe the Greatest" Roberts (SLH) decided to do a 'Clarke'. He burst away from the field,which included our own Mel Thorpe,and really looked most impressive. Unfortunately he could only keep it up for a few laps before the bunch caught him again. Then Barry Collins (Surrey AC) made a break and he managed to hold out just long enough to win. At one time he had a lead of 30y but Mel,finishing very strongly,all but caught the Surrey man on the tape. After qualifying fairly easily in the 'half' heats,Danny Wiseman got up to 4th in the final with 1:56.0 . He started racing rather late this season due to injuries but is now improving every time out and should be back to peak form before very long. items.s: Thresher & Dear Excel at 'RYDER' Report and results of the Ryder meeting at Southampton Sports Centre on 3 July, where John Thresher ran a best 880 yards and John Dear won the 3000m steeplechase, with Gerry North winning the 3 miles. July 3rd - Southampton Sports Centre Our overall performance at the Southampton meeting was as usual pretty dreadful.Surely we can produce better results at trophy meetings than this. Before long we are going to find ourselves excluded as we were from the"Kinnaird" a few years back. Getting away from this more dismal side though,there were several bright spots. John Thresher ran a powerful 880 yards to finish 3rd in his best ever time. Passing the bell in 55secs,he didn't really start moving through the field until the final bend,finishing very strongly and improving on his position all the way up the straight. He later ran an excellent relay leg in the medley taking us from last (20 yards down on the nearest team) to 2nd with an unofficial time of 1:54.6. This new found speed is all John needs to duck under four minutes for the mile. All this year John Dear has been hovering around 10 minutes for the 3000m Steeplechase,but at last he has broken through, He started steadily working his way up the field until with three laps to go he found himself in the lead. Quickly opening a gap,he kept the pace going throughout those last and usually for John,fatal,laps. Only one other runner managed to close the gap at all,but John's effort had been well timed and he finished with 10 yards to spare, slashing his personal best by 20 seconds. John's hurdling technique is nigh-on perfect and with just a little more strength to tide him over those last few laps he could prove a difficult man to beat. 220y'A'1.D.Dear(Sthampton)22.5 6.C.Brooks(BELS) 23.2 440y'A'7.D.Wiseman(BELS) 'B'5.A.Mead (BELS) 53.0 120yH 1.L.Taitt (HHH) 14.7 4.P.Pepe (BELS) 16.3 3000mSC1.J.Dear (BELS) 9:40.0 Jav.2.N.Head (BELS) 194'0½" PV E.Stanghon (BELS) 10'0" 220x220x440x880 1.Blackheath 3:32.2 2.BELGRAVE H 3:37.9 880y'A'1.K.Bromley(Walton) 1:51.6 2.P.Kilford(Ports) 1:51.6 3.J.Thresher (BELS) 1:52.3 1 m'A' Geoff North(BELS) dnf 'B' 1.L.O'Hara (BELS) 4:19.9 2.J.Baldwin(Blackheath) 4:21.0 3m 1.Gerry North (BELS) 13:47.0 2.W.Kerr (BELS) 14:05.4 3.J.Baldwin (Blackheath)14:09.6 John Thresher John Thresher John Thresher John J.Thresher John Dear John Dear John Dear John J.Dear D. items.sum: Report and results of the Brockman Trophy meeting at Wimbledon Park on 17 July, where Mel Thorpe became the 7th Belgravian under 14 minutes for 3 miles and Belgrave were 8th.
items.s: BROCKMAN TROPHY: Good times by Thorpe and Wiseman Report and results of the Brockman Trophy meeting at Wimbledon Park on 17 July, where Mel Thorpe became the 7th Belgravian under 14 minutes for 3 miles and Belgrave were 8th. July 17th - Wimbledon Park Danny Wiseman qualified for the final in the first heat of the half with no trouble in 1:56.0. In the other heat,however,Varah of Hercules took it into his head to go for a fast time. He succeeded alright,so shaking up the field that Huffer (TVH) didn't even qualify. The final was a great race with Danny hovering in 3rd or 4th place after a fast start,the bell being reached in 57.1 He dropped back slightly during the third furlong but down the straight he fought his way through to take 3rd place in his fastest time this year. Cliff 'Snowy' Brooks reached the 100 yards final and finished 6th in 10.5, triple jumped 44'1¼",to place 4th and also competed in the 220y and Long Jump- not a bad afternoons work. In the 3 miles 'Kipper' Herring of Blackheath was in a class apart from the rest of the field,beating the championship best by 20secs. The race for the minor positions was a different kettle of fish though,Barry Collins and Bob Holt just managing to get away from Mel Thorpe in the latter stages. Mel hung on very well after passing 2 miles in 9:13 to record 13:55.8 and become the 7th Belgravian to beat 14 minutes this year. TeeKay Hart put up a solid performance in the '6' and looked fairly comfortable in running 29:30.0. He should improve still further on this in the Club '6'. John Bicourt and Peter Pepe both ran well,John being beaten by two good men in the 3000m SC and Pete finishing 5th in the high hurdles final. It may seem a little early with this season not yet over,but how about trying to clean up at the 'Brockman' next year. With many of our excellent junior sprinters and field events men becoming seniors,we could have a finalist in EVERY event. Walton,Blackheath,etc do well in trophy meets,why shouldn't we. Lets have EVERYONE turning out for this meeting next year - Please. 100y 1.A.Tymms (Surrey) 9.9 2.M.Yardley(Walton)10.0 6.C.Brooks (BEL) 10.5 3m 1.J.Herring (Blackheath H)13:27.6 2.B.Collins (Surrey) 13:52.6 3.R.Holt (Hercules) 13:54.8 4.M.Thorpe (BEL) 13:55.8 6m 1.B.Ellis(TVH) 29:12.4 2.G.Taylor(Camb) 29:20.0 3.T.Hart(BEL) 29:30.0 880y 1.M.Varah (Hercules) 1:52.6 2.D.Wright (Blackheath H) 1:52.8 3.D.Wiseman (BEL) 1:53.8 120yH 1.L.Taitt(HHH) 14.4 2.G.Tymms(Surrey) 15.1 5.P.Pepe (BEL) 16.1 TJ 4.C.Brooks (BEL) 44'1¼" 3000mSC1.G.Pymm (TVH) 9:15.8 2.D.Gibson (Surrey)9:22.6 3.J.Bicourt(BEL) 9:34.8 TEAM : 8.BELGRAVE H 22pts Danny Wiseman Danny Wiseman Danny Wiseman Danny D.Wiseman M. items.sum: Report and results of the all-age match against Surrey AC and Herne Hill at Norbiton on 27 July, won by Belgrave, including John Bicourt's first go at the hammer.
items.s: July 27th - Norbiton v Surrey AC, Herne Hill H. Report and results of the all-age match against Surrey AC and Herne Hill at Norbiton on 27 July, won by Belgrave, including John Bicourt's first go at the hammer. In this match,where all age groups score for an overall result,we had easily the best turnout so far this year - mainly due to so many younger members being present. The very satisfying result was that we beat Surrey AC in their own territory. Bill Couzens had his finest Javelin throw for some years and also found a new toy-the Hammer. This latter event also provided the biggest laugh of the year when John Bicourt decided to have a go,"Just to score a point". On his first throw he forgot to let go,his second scattered the officials when the weight came off the end,but his third and only legal throw sailed clear over several markers to place him 3rd. 100y 2.C.Ryan 10.3 4.C.Brooks 10.6 'B'1.J.Vivian 10.0 220y 3.C.Ryan 23.5 4.C.Brooks 23.6 120yH 4.P.Pepe 16.5 440y 4.A.Mead 53.5 880y 3.J.Bicourt 2:02.0 5.J.Hampshire 2:07.0 1m 1.M.Thorpe 4:16.0 3.J.Bicourt 4:24.0 Jav 1.W.Couzens 162'7¾" 2.B.King 160'5½" LJ 3.C.Brooks 21'3' HJ 3.C.Brooks 5'6" Shot 3.B.King 31'8¾" 6.W.Couzens 30'0¼" 1.BELGRAVE H 205pts 2.Surrey AC 197pts 3.Herne Hill H 122pts Bill Couzens Bill Couzens Bill Couzens W.Couzens John Bicourt John Bicourt John Bicourt J.Bicourt C. items.sum: Note that John Hilton is the first member to gain the new 2nd class Road Running Standard, with the qualifying times.
items.s: Note that John Hilton is the first member to gain the new 2nd class Road Running Standard, with the qualifying times. By his runs in the Mitcham '15',Epsom '10' and Finchley '20' John Hilton became the first member to obtain the newly instituted 2nd class Road Running Standard. For those who may not know what this standard is details are as follows:- To attain any three of the following times in the same calendar year 10miles - 63:00 15miles - 98:00 20miles - 2:15:00 Marathon - 3:15:0 Races like the Romford Half-Marathon,Chichester - Portsmouth '16' will be converted to the nearest of the above distances. items.s: The Polytechnic Marathon Report and result of the Polytechnic Marathon on 12 June, won by Shigematsu in a world best, with Belgrave second team and John Moore taking the club championship. June 12th In ideal conditions the race was won by M.Shigematsu of Japan in a world's best time of 2hrs.12mins. The Belgrave team was smaller than for many years but performed well to take second team medals in the open race (6 teams closed in). For once we had the better of the last scorers and so just beat Hornchurch for second place. Charlie Walker was well up at the start but possibly misjudged the pace. After going through 15miles in just over 84mins. he began to slow down quite a bit and John Moore, now beginning to get a little fitter, passed Charlie at about 21 miles and went on to take the Belgrave Championship Geoff Pearson and John Hilton ran well throughout John finishing in a personal best time. Brian Nott, running for Ranelagh, ran a 'blinder' to finish 12th in 2:27:56. Had he not been a second claim member this would have been a new Club Record. 122 started. July 17th - Wimbledon In this very high standard race the first five broke Fred Norris' record, the first eighteen were inside AAA Grade I standards and the first thirty-seven (a third of the starters) were inside two hours. Bob Roath,Jim Derham,F.Maillardet and Ian Macintosh were together for the first sixteen miles and it was only in the last four miles that this quartet began to split,Bob Roath proving the strongest. From the Belgrave point of view it was encouraging to see Chris Steer running so well and John Moore now getting slowly back to somewhere near his best. Charlie Walker ran very well for the first fifteen miles but then tired badly. 113 started,88 finished,14 teams closed in. items.sum: Note on four Belgrave juniors at the AAA Junior Championships on 7 August, where Jim Vivian set a club 100 yards record of 9.9.
items.s: Note on four Belgrave juniors at the AAA Junior Championships on 7 August, where Jim Vivian set a club 100 yards record of 9.9. We had four athletes good enough to perform in the AAA Junior Champs on August 7th, and what fine efforts they were too! Jim Vivian chalked up a Belgrave record of 9.9secs for the short sprint, and although losing by inches to Nash of South Africa he had the consolation of being the fastest Englishman. Later he was a fine 4th in the longer sprint with 22.5. Although a foot below his best for the season, John Mitchell finished 4th in the Long jump with 22'-2¾". Martin (22.9) was unlucky to be eliminated in a 220 heat with such a good time, as was Gleeson (51.3) in the 440. items.s: Note on the Crystal Palace evening meeting on 17 August, where Bill Kerr gashed his leg before the 2 miles and Mike Shingles helped Belgrave win the team race. Disaster struck for Bill Kerr at the Crystal Palace evening meeting on August 17th. Whilst attempting to vault a wall just before the start of the 2 miles he slipped, fell and gashed his leg sufficiently badly to go to hospital for stitching. How fortunate we were to have the greatly improved Mike Shingles at hand to act as 3rd scorer. He clocked a personal best 9:19 and Belgrave clinched a team win by 6 points from Blackheath and 10 points from T.V.H. The race winner was International Fergus Murray (8:40) followed by internationals Herring and Green. Gerry North was 5th in 8:58 and Laurie O'Hara (still trying hard to duck under 9 mins) 7th in 9:03.4. items.label: November 1965
items.sum: Christmas editorial hailing the quality and depth of Belgrave's 1965 track and field rankings, crediting the coaches, and noting Ray Middleton's Tommy Green Cup and Edgar Horton cup awards.
items.s: EDITORIAL Christmas editorial hailing the quality and depth of Belgrave's 1965 track and field rankings, crediting the coaches, and noting Ray Middleton's Tommy Green Cup and Edgar Horton cup awards. We wish all our members a MERRY CHRISTMAS and a HAPPY NEW YEAR. Before crossing the threshold of 1966, though we would suggest you cast more than a passing glance at our back page, which lists the best track and field performances of 1965. Compared with three or four years ago these lists are a revelation. Although some events are a little weak there is an overall picture of quality and depth that is deeply satisfying. Certain performances and events stand out. In the three miles we had no less than 7 men breaking the magical 14 mins, yet it seems only yesterday that the great Sydney Wooderson became the first Briton to achieve this feat. Six men over 20'-0" in the long jump and the leading two still Juniors! Eight sprinters doing 10.5 or better and only two of them Seniors! Our record-breaking AAA junior 4x110 relay quartet that made the opposition look mediocre---one could soon run out of superlatives if all events were appraised. What is the reason for such progress? Well, there is little doubt that the advance of our sprinters and jumpers is very largely due to the expert handling of Ben Lulham and that long-jumper-turned-coach, Dave Ansell. Thanks to the enthusiastic attention of George Piddington, our coaching Honorary Secretary, there is also more co-ordination now amongst the coaches and greater efforts made to help those in the cinderella events. The prospects for the future are indeed limitless. 1965 could be the year that started it all. * * * Once again that outstanding walker, Ray Middleton, has been awarded the "Tommy Green" Cup for the year's most meritorious performance. As National 50 Kilos champion he richly deserved our highest award. The Race Walking Association also acknowledged his championship win by awarding him the "Edgar Horton" cup. Our walkers are indeed fortunate to have calibre of this sort around which to re-build those mighty teams of a few years back. Sydney Wooderson Sydney Wooderson Ben Lulham Ben Lulham Dave Ansell Dave Ansell George Piddington George Piddington Ray Middleton Ray Middleton AAA Junior Championships 1965 National 50 Kilometres Walk Championship 1965 Race Walking Association

items.label: November 1965
items.sum: The Hon. Secretary's notes covering the death of Mrs. R.W. Ricketts, AGM honours, the 1966 club championships date, the Norths' Mexico City trip, the AAA junior relay win, the London v Milan match, winter hopes and new members.
items.s: HON SEC'S NOTES The Hon. Secretary's notes covering the death of Mrs. R.W. Ricketts, AGM honours, the 1966 club championships date, the Norths' Mexico City trip, the AAA junior relay win, the London v Milan match, winter hopes and new members. We all regret the news of the passing of Mrs.R.W.Ricketts, a Vice - President of the Club for many years, and widow of Bob Ricketts, our dynamic President in the early 1920's. Bob's personality and ability undoubtedly gave the club the leadership it needed in the years immediately following the first World War; and was the main contribution to the Belgrave sequence of growing successes which eventually brought National Championships to the Club, and a national reputation. In all his work he had the full support, and the sacrifice, of his wife and family; and their contribution was a very real one indeed. The Ricketts family gave us the "Belgrave Cup", the Ricketts Shield, the Ricketts Cup, and the "Doris"Shield - and to that same Doris, the daughter, we offer our thanks and sympathy on the recent death of her Mother. * * * At the Annual General Meeting we honoured ourselves by electing to Life Membership FRANK JARVIS (Asst.Hon.Secretary and a great worker for a number of years) and TED STIMPSON (International runner, Club Officer and our present Social Hon.Secretary); and adding to our list of Vice-Presidents STAN DAVIES, JACK HAMPSHIRE (Snr) and BEN LULHAM all of whom have been and continue to be, great workers for the Club. * * * Our Club Track and Field Championships have been provisionally booked at Hurlingham Track on Saturday, 4th June 1966. All Club athletes are asked to note this date immediately and to ensure that they will be able to participate when the Championships come along and not be committed elsewhere. Club officials and supporters are similarly asked to make a note of this important date. * * * Our good wishes go with Gerry and Geoff North who have been invited to go to Mexico City with a small party of athletes and doctors on a British Olympic Association mission to study the problems of acclimatisation and of competition at 7,500 feet above sea level, as a prelude to the Olympic Games to be held in Mexico City in 1968. We hope our lads will enjoy their trip and return ready to take first and second place in the Southern and English Cross-Country Championships in their stride. * * * How proud we were - those of us who had the privilege of being at Hurlingham Park Track - to see our Junior sprint relay team have a magnificent win in the AAA Championships. The style and power of our lads' running impressed everyone and gave us future visions of Senior relay Championships to be won! And here let us give praise to the man behind the win - Ben Lulham - whose coaching and encouragement has made such a memorable season possible. * * * It was good to see at the AGM a number of our younger members present and a good sprinkling of those who have worked hard for the club in years gone by. We were particularly glad to welcome Past President Syd Roberts after a critical illness from which he is now making a fast recovery, Jimmy Flatt a Club cross-country Champion of the 1920's, Charlie Speechley who joined us in 1919 and almost ever-present Harry Evans who won an RWA Championship (and led home the second team) as far back as 1908. * * * We provided three members of the London team which visited Milan recently to compete against a Lombardy team as part of the British Trade Fair Week. They were John Thresher,who won the 1,500 metres event; Derek Boosey,second in the Triple Jump and fourth in the Long Jump; and Gerry North, third in the 10,000 metres event,(In this race a new Italian record was set up by the winner, Ambu);but the London team had an easy win in the overall match. * * * We should be due this winter for a return to Championship winning form over the country. The Surrey, the South of Thames Senior, the Southern and the English could all provide Belgrave wins - They have done so in the past! And while we are at it, let's make a determined effort to win also the special trophies awarded to the clubs who finish their complete team of runners in the most forward positions. These are an index of strength and depth and should well suit our teams. * * * We have welcomed a great number of new members in recent months and we wish them happiness and success in our colours. A particular welcome to David Mayo, a young schoolmaster from U.S.A , who has come to our country to learn all about Walking and to raise himself to International level of performance. We wish him well and will watch his improvement toward his goal with great interest. A.A.H. Mrs. R.W. items.label: November 1965
items.sum: Profile of new club President Bob Taylor, tracing his half-mile and mile running career from 1950, his illness, and his service as Track Captain and Track Secretary.
items.s: The President Profile of new club President Bob Taylor, tracing his half-mile and mile running career from 1950, his illness, and his service as Track Captain and Track Secretary. Bob Taylor, our President for 1965/66, was persuaded to join the Club in 1949 by one Chas. Walker; both being buddies in the Royal Signals. Although Bob had dabbled in the sport of athletics for some while it wasn't until 1950, after his first winter of REAL training, that he gave any hint of the things to come, with a 3rd place in the Club 1 mile Champ., 2nd in the LCC mile and 12th in the South of the Thames Junior Cross Country. By 1952 he was really moving and apart from making the final of the AAA 880 yards, he collected a fistful of medals, being placed in the Middlesex, Civil Service, City Charity and Brockman Trophy 'halfs' and winning the Club Champs. and Heathfield Trophy at the same distance. Nor did he confine his activities to the track for he was also a member of our very successful 'Brighton' team that won the Southern and came 2nd in the National London-Brighton Road Relay that year. The following season brought even more success when Bob won nearly all these events and more. His dedication in training and determination in racing made him an athlete to be feared. Any lesser mortal would have been satisfied with this sort of progress, but not so Bob. He reckoned that by switching his distance to the mile he had a good chance of making the international team for the 1954 European and Empire Games. His times alone will show how close he was to his goal:- 880y - 1:53.6 ¾ mile - 3:00.8 1 mile - 4:14.0 (on the Drayton Green track!). Remember this is 1954! Unhappily for Bob,and athletics in general, illness struck and it was three years before he could run again. Even then he managed to regain his Club title at 880 yards, but Bob was always one to give his all in racing and he decided that without the training, he would do himself more harm than good, so he called it a day. He had already been Track Captain since 1956 so when the Track Secretary's job became vacant in 1962, Bob was the obvious successor. A great Club man, whether he be encouraging our teams, leading the 'Brighton' choir, coaching the youngsters or helping to organise our various social activities, Bob Taylor does US honour by becoming our President. And it still takes a fit man to beat him down to Tibbets Corner and back. Bob Taylor Bob Taylor Bob Taylor Bob Chas. Walker Chas. items.s: A Word From Your President New President Bob Taylor thanks members for electing him and sends Christmas wishes and hopes for a successful year. I should like to take this opportunity to express my sincere thanks for the great honour you have paid me by electing me as your President for the coming year. Every President hopes that the Club will have a successful year and so far our senior runners have started the winter season with some excellent performances. I am sure that there are greater things to come, for success breeds the success which I hope will spread throughout the Club. We have the athletes and officials in every section of the Club to once again achieve the highest honours in the sport. Together, I hope we can make this a year to remember in the history of the Club. Wishing you all a very Merry Christmas and Best Wishes for the coming year. Yours Sincerely Bob Taylor Bob Taylor Bob Taylor

items.label: November 1965
items.sum: Report of the Belgrave Harriers Annual General Meeting of 22nd September 1965, lamenting low attendance and recording deaths, the Secretary's report, the accounts, life memberships, junior honours and Robert Taylor's election as President.
items.s: A. G. M. Report of the Belgrave Harriers Annual General Meeting of 22nd September 1965, lamenting low attendance and recording deaths, the Secretary's report, the accounts, life memberships, junior honours and Robert Taylor's election as President. Wednesday, 22nd September, 1965 was the day chosen for the Belgrave Harriers' Annual General Meeting. The Notice of the Meeting together with the agenda was circulated to all members ( approx. 500) as is required by the Rules of the Club. So it was that the President, Jack Goswell, stood and waited for the Belgravians to attend their own particular Meeting; whereat much information could be gathered and valuable contacts made. To summarize, a meeting to examine the account of the year's work carried out by the Committee on behalf of Belgrave Harriers; the development of the particular branch of athletics of any individual member; the facilities made for his advancement and for the furtherance of athletics in general. It is an inalienable right of every Belgravian that he can attend the Annual General Meeting of the Club to investigate its management. Of the approx 500 members only about 75 to 80 made the journey to Belgrave Hall for the meeting. When it is remembered that the average attendance at the monthly committee meetings is 35 and that it is reasonable to think that the full number of 41 committee members were present, it indicates that about 40 members were interested in the development of Athletics carried out by the Belgrave Harriers. It could be said, of course, that the method of managing the affairs of the Club gives satisfaction to the majority of its members and that it was unnecessary to attend the meeting. This reasoning may be one of comfort to any committee, but good administration depends on criticism and watchfulness, and questions from the 'floor' are invigorating. The meeting was opened by the President and the business of the Belgrave Harriers commenced. The deaths of Mrs. Ricketts ( Vice-President), T. Askew and C. Warren were reported, this part of an Annual General Meeting always strikes a sombre note, contributing to the history of the Club as it does by the passing of the torch of the Belgrave Harriers ideals from the Elder Belgravian to the young Belgravian. The Club is proud of its history and of its approach to Athletics. In making his report to the meeting, the Secretary, Alf. Harley commented on the performances of members in their various fields of athletics. The improving prowess of the Juniors and the winning of the Southern Counties A.A.A. 4 by 110 yards Junior Relay Championship. Mention was made of the various activities carried out by the Social committee and a special word of thanks was due to Mrs. Savage, together with Mrs. W. Shepherd and Mrs Hampshire for their efforts and hard work in providing a catering service of a very high standard to members and visitors at Belgrave Hall on all possible occasions. The Committee believed that a debt of thanks was owing to all the ladies for their assistance to Belgrave Harriers. The presentation of the financial accounts was worthy of notice inasmuch that the accounts had been audited by two chartered accountants and the mass of figures had been reduced to a state of simplicity and understanding much appreciated by the members present. The business of the meeting proceeded without incident; the election of two Life-Members - F. Jarvis and E. Stimpson, the award of Junior Honours Badges to J.Vivian J. Martin, D. Gleeson and C. Oliver as members of the successful Junior Relay team mentioned above. Robert Taylor was elected President of the Club for the ensuing year and the other Offices were duly filled. To a new member it would appear that Officers are elected as though pre-destined for Office; no one opposes; no other nominations are made. No Officer is pre-destined,but someone has to do the work, and until the new man comes along, the work will continue . Amanuensis Jack Goswell Jack Goswell Mrs. Ricketts Mrs. Ricketts T. Askew T. items.h: TRACK & FIELD ROUND-UP — Vivian beats even time
items.sum: Report of the AAA Junior Championships at Hurlingham on 7th August 1965, where Jim Vivian ran 9.9 for 100 yards but lost the title to South African Paul Nash, with results.
items.s: TRACK & FIELD ROUND-UP — Vivian beats even time Report of the AAA Junior Championships at Hurlingham on 7th August 1965, where Jim Vivian ran 9.9 for 100 yards but lost the title to South African Paul Nash, with results. TRACK & FIELD ROUND-UP August 7th - Hurlingham - AAA JUNIOR CHAMPIONSHIPS Vivian beats even time Jim Vivian had the galling experience of beating all British contenders, underlining the fact that he is the best Junior 'dash' specialist in the country, yet losing the AAA title to South African, Paul Nash. Jim's time of 9.9 secs was a personal best which equals our Senior Club Record and shatters the Junior mark by 2 tenths. He was also 4th in the final of the furlong (3rd Briton) and should have no difficulty in taking both these events next year when he is still eligible. In the Long Jump, John Mitchell had trouble in trying to pull out that 'big one' and was a foot below his best, nevertheless finishing 4th just behind yet another South African. After taking up the 'quarter' only halfway through the season, Denis Gleeson now has a best time of 51.3. With a little extra strength gained during this winter, next season should see him under 50.0 and providing the nucleus of a decent Senior 4 x 440y team. items.sum: Report of Danny's 800m silver for Britain at the Maccabiah Games in Tel-Aviv, August 1965, with a note on his rise from sprinter to middle-distance runner.
items.s: DANNY BRINGS HOME A 'SILVER' Report of Danny's 800m silver for Britain at the Maccabiah Games in Tel-Aviv, August 1965, with a note on his rise from sprinter to middle-distance runner. August 26th/31st - Tel-Aviv MACCABIAH GAMES Running in the 800m, Danny clocked an impressive 1:52.5 to take 2nd place for Britain behind Herrmann (USA) who won in record time. He also ran in the 1500m,finishing in 4:04.2 (approx.4:22 for 1 mile). Three years ago Dan was just a mediocre sprinter who found he had more success over the 'quarter',managing to win the Surrey junior. Later the same season he scrounged a run in an invitation 880y and duly won, beating several more fancied rivals. Since then he has improved steadily and could in the next few years become one of the 'greats' over 880yards and 1 mile. Danny Danny Danny Dan Herrmann Herrmann Maccabiah Games 1965 Surrey Junior Championships Tel-Aviv USA

items.s: BELGRAVE WIN AAA 4x110y J Report of Belgrave's junior 4x110 yards win at the AAA Relay Championships at Hurlingham on 28th August 1965, with the relay and invitation 3 miles results. August 28th - Hurlingham - AAA RELAY CHAMPIONSHIPS BELGRAVE WIN AAA 4x110y J On this dull day at Hurlingham, our Juniors more than made up for the fact that we could not muster a single team in the Senior events (not even for the 4x1 mile). They qualified for the final convincingly, but in the other heat Surrey AC put up a faster time, making it plain that they would not let this championship slip by without a fight. In the final, John Mitchell rocketed away from the gun and even at the first take-over the Bels had a substantial lead. With brilliant baton passing, Denis Gleeson and Chris Martin put us even further ahead and when Jim Vivian took the baton for the last leg it was all over. By winning this event the Bels have made a clean sweep of all Junior relay championships this year, breaking two county records and beating the AAA best champ. performance with a time that ranks third best in the country (including Senior club teams). Please spare a thought though for our reserve, Clive Oliver, who would be the star of any normal team. Indeed it has been rumoured that at our present strength we could take on any two combined teams in an 8 x 110 yards race. Pos Team Time 1. BELGRAVE HARRIERS 42.8 (AAA Champ.BP) 2.
